title: Consume Ratconfig UI revision c6ee666
description:
## Why

Yazelix still packages Ratconfig revision `5883db3`, so the config popup does not contain the published Unicode-width correction, light-mode contrast fixes, darker inactive tabs and pane headings, or simplified pane chrome through `c6ee666`. Yazelix owns the pinned child revision and product-level Mars dogfooding.

## Evidence

- `flake.nix:50-53` declares Ratconfig as a non-flake GitHub input.
- `flake.lock:281-295` locks Ratconfig to `5883db3a40f81dc886a7f557d8c7b2c33097147e`.
- Published Ratconfig commits after that pin are `e755d9f` (Unicode field-column widths), `dc0e8bb` (light-mode contrast), and `c6ee666` (light-mode tabs/titles and pane-border polish); `95539c2` is the intervening child-ledger closure.
- Closed Yazelix bead `yazelix-5vl-mq4` records the ownership split: Ratconfig owns renderer semantics; Yazelix owns the dependency pin and product integration.

## User-Visible Contract

The packaged config popup consumes Ratconfig `c6ee666`: light appearance keeps semantic text readable, inactive tabs and the `settings`/`details` headings render black, selected semantic colors remain intact, Unicode setting labels retain correct terminal-cell alignment, and the two body panes use flush outer rails plus one shared vertical divider without top/bottom pane rails. Dark appearance remains readable and otherwise unchanged.

## Scope

In scope:
- Update only the Ratconfig input lock to exact revision `c6ee6662013afd2d832c391d206d63ff1f6c8c1f` while preserving concurrent lockfile work.
- Run the Yazelix flake, package, temporary-profile, and config-popup integration checks against the remote child revision with no local override.
- Dogfood the normal transparent popup in Mars light and dark appearance, including tabs, pane headings, selected/error rows, structured details, Unicode labels, narrow width, outer rails, and the shared divider.
- Explicitly judge whether the tab row remains sufficiently separated from the borderless pane headings. If it is ambiguous, capture the runtime view and return to the maintainer before choosing any separator treatment.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` for the visible popup behavior and refresh the README LOC scorecard as required by repository policy.
- Refresh the installed Yazelix profile after the verified runtime-flake change.

Out of scope:
- Do not edit Ratconfig source, copy its palette/layout into Yazelix, vendor it, or use a committed local-path override.
- Do not change Mars colors, transparency, the 50/50 pane split, config schema, validation, file IO, or apply behavior.
- Do not invent a replacement horizontal separator without maintainer approval after dogfooding.
- Do not update unrelated flake inputs.

## Implementation Notes

1. Record the pre-existing dirty `flake.lock` diff, then update only the Ratconfig input and verify the resulting locked revision exactly.
2. Inspect the lock diff before running checks; retain every unrelated user-owned change.
3. Run automated integration from the remote lock, then install through a temporary profile.
4. Dogfood both appearances. Treat the missing tab/body divider as an explicit visual experiment, not an already-settled design contract.
5. Update current-state documentation and the LOC scorecard without migration-style prose.
6. Upgrade the user profile only after all package and manual checks pass.

## Verification

- `jq -r '.nodes.ratconfig.locked.rev' flake.lock` prints `c6ee6662013afd2d832c391d206d63ff1f6c8c1f`.
- `nix flake check` exits 0.
- `nix flake show --all-systems` exits 0.
- `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` exits 0.
- `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` exits 0 and the temporary install uses the remote locked child.
- Manual Mars light-mode dogfooding confirms tab/title contrast, semantic selected-row contrast, Unicode alignment, and the simplified three-rail pane geometry; dark-mode dogfooding finds no regression.
- `nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix` succeeds after acceptance.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if updating Ratconfig would overwrite or entangle unrelated in-progress `flake.lock` changes; isolate the single input update first.
- Stop if the lock resolves to a different Ratconfig revision; inspect the child range rather than silently consuming extra commits.
- Stop and return with a screenshot if removing the horizontal pane rails makes the tab-to-body boundary unclear; do not choose a replacement separator autonomously.
- Stop if integration requires Yazelix-owned copies of Ratconfig styles/layout or a Mars palette change.
- Stop if any automated gate fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable focused fix.

## Maintenance Notes

- Dependency decision: update the existing pinned Ratconfig input only; add no package, crate, adapter, or second style owner.
- Effort S. Risk LOW/MED because automated ownership is narrow but final acceptance depends on transparent runtime rendering. Confidence HIGH.
- Child reference: `ratconfig-light-mode-contrast-nh8`; published revision: `c6ee6662013afd2d832c391d206d63ff1f6c8c1f`.
- Rejected alternatives: vendoring Ratconfig, a local-path production override, duplicating theme roles in Yazelix, weakening the selected-row contract, and preemptively restoring a horizontal rail before runtime review.
notes: Implementation staged against exact Ratconfig revision c6ee6662013afd2d832c391d206d63ff1f6c8c1f. Checked remote tip first: origin/main is b9844f2 and contains c6ee666, but also introduces the separately gated Core/All public API while ratconfig-core-all-settings-5d9.3 remains open, so tip adoption was rejected for this visual-only bead. The lock diff changes only Ratconfig from 5883db3 to c6ee666. Added current-state CHANGELOG wording and corrected the reproducible scorecard to 18,217 lines; the prior Rust count was stale by two lines after rustfmt. Verification passed: exact revision assertion, git diff check, nix flake check with all 40 yzx-config tests, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, temporary-profile install/status, and installed runtime refresh. Manual light/dark Mars dogfooding remains before closure.
close_reason: Completed: pinned Ratconfig c6ee666, all automated integration gates passed, and maintainer dogfooding confirmed the light/dark contrast, Unicode alignment, and simplified pane geometry.

title: Coordinate adaptive Yazelix appearance
description: Coordinate one persisted Yazelix `appearance.mode` across component-owned adapters. Root configuration owns exact dark/light intent and Ratconfig presentation. Mars receives that intent independently through its existing configuration contract. Zellij owns a configurable native dark/light pair and receives the same root intent through native actions for fresh and current managed sessions. The Zellij model is pair-only: inherited ansi/gruvbox-light, no static fixed override, and no persisted active member. Yazi, Ghostty, auto/system mode, and CSI 2031 interoperability remain separate later work.
design:
Ownership and data flow:

1. Root `appearance.mode` is the only persisted managed dark/light intent.
2. Yazelix projects that intent independently to Mars native configuration and the intended Zellij session.
3. Zellij owns `theme_dark` and `theme_light`, resolves the selected member, and emits its actual committed mode.
4. The child-owned Yazelix bar has one runtime template and two internal palettes; it follows the Zellij mode event rather than receiving a second root transport.

The paired palettes are not public presets. Rejected: one fixed hex palette because transparent dark and light backgrounds require different contrast; one ANSI-only palette because it makes integrated appearance terminal-dependent and less deterministic; separate public bar presets because they add configuration and synchronization state; direct root-to-bar fan-out because it can diverge from the actual Zellij mode; Mars as control plane, CSI 2031 as root intent, a polling daemon, and a generic theme bus because each adds the wrong authority or more machinery than the contract needs.

The shared Zellij theme pool remains intentional until user evidence justifies curated dark and light classifications. Pair-only following remains intentional; a future fixed override would require an explicit third follow/fixed state and is outside this epic.
acceptance_criteria: One Core dark/light control applies independently to Mars and the current managed Zellij session at launch and live. Zellij uses its inherited or explicit pair without a third selector or competing static theme. Home Manager ownership is truthful, partial live failure never rolls back saved intent, focused and flake checks pass, and maintainer dogfood confirms dark-to-light-to-dark readability. No generic fan-out framework, palette registry, polling daemon, or Mars-as-control-plane is introduced.
notes: Execution remains split across child beads: `.1` authority, `.2` Mars projection, `.3` Ratconfig cutover, `.4` final pair choice, `.5` pair persistence/materialization, `.7` live and fresh Zellij projection, `.8` structural initial/live bar palette parity, and `.6` final end-to-end verification. Final Zellij decisions supersede earlier comments: one shared packaged/custom pool, ansi dark default, gruvbox-light light default, pair-only following, and legacy static `theme` preserved on disk but ignored at runtime. The bar exposes one template with two internal palettes, not separate presets. Yazi, Ghostty, auto/system mode, and CSI 2031 remain non-blocking related work.
close_reason: All scoped appearance architecture, implementation, parity, and end-to-end verification beads are complete.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Architecture decisions completed 2026-07-25: appearance.mode is the only persisted managed authority, with exact dark/light values and sparse default dark. Managed Mars and the current Zellij session receive independent projections; partial live failure never rolls back intent. Unmanaged terminals are not controlled. Home Manager uses programs.yazelix.config.settings.appearance.mode, stays read-only in Ratconfig, and applies next launch. Mars native appearance remains standalone-only/read-only discovery. Selected inherited Zellij pair: gruvbox-dark / gruvbox-light; static themes remain fixed overrides.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Supersedes comment 19 where it conflicts with the implemented contract. Final review on 2026-07-25/26 confirms: the inherited Zellij pair is ansi / gruvbox-light, there is no fixed static override, and the bar uses one public runtime template with two internal contrast palettes. A single fixed hex palette was rejected because it cannot remain reliably readable over both transparent dark and light backgrounds; an ANSI-only palette remains a valid smaller alternative but would make integrated appearance terminal-dependent. Bead .8 owns structural launch/live bar field parity, then .6 owns final composed dogfood.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Final integration gate .6 passed and is closed. The appearance epic now has one persisted Core dark/light authority, independent Mars and exact-session native Zellij projection, inherited or explicit Zellij theme pairs, structurally shared initial/live bar palettes, truthful partial failure, Home Manager ownership, green full checks, positive maintainer dogfood, and a refreshed installed runtime. Stable remains untouched.

title: Lock the explicit dark/light appearance contract
description:
## Why

Yazelix root configuration, not Mars, owns one desired product appearance; managed backends apply it and applications own their dark/light theme pairs. This decision fixes the remaining precedence, persistence, live-failure, unmanaged-host, Home Manager, and inventory semantics before implementation.

## Evidence

- `defaults/config.toml` is the packaged semantic root, and `crates/yzx-config/src/root_config.rs` already derives sparse user intent over packaged defaults.
- `runtime/yzx/runtime.rs:92-160,230-310` owns launch configuration and backend environment projection.
- Mars accepts `MARS_APPEARANCE` over `[mars.appearance].preset` for package consumers.
- `home-manager/module.nix:105-176` renders `programs.yazelix.config.settings` to the root `config.toml`.
- `crates/yzx-config/src/paths.rs:32-76` and `model.rs:687-720` already recognize store-backed Home Manager sources, make them read-only, and provide exact switch guidance.
- The pinned Zellij fork exposes native dark/light pair fields and direct `set-dark-theme` / `set-light-theme` actions.
- Complete Mars inventory bead `yazelix-5vl-core-all-config-discovery-lsw.3` must remain complete without presenting a second managed appearance authority.

## Final decision

1. Schema and default
   - Root path is `appearance.mode`. The initial values are exactly `dark` and `light`.
   - The packaged default is `dark`; an absent sparse value inherits dark. Resetting the field returns to that default and applies dark.
   - Invalid root values are source errors: no live projection runs and no fallback value is persisted.
   - `auto` and system following are deferred. Adding either reopens the authority and transport decision; there is no alias or hidden third value.

2. Precedence
   - In a managed Yazelix session, root `appearance.mode` is authoritative for every opted-in managed adapter.
   - A valid native `[mars.appearance].preset` remains user-owned and meaningful for standalone Mars, but managed `yzx launch` overrides it without importing, synchronizing, deleting, or rewriting it.
   - A conflicting native value is explained on its read-only discovery row rather than warned on every launch. A syntactically or semantically invalid native file remains a native source error that must be repaired; the root value does not mask parser failure.
   - Future Ghostty support must use explicit consent and the same root authority; it may not import Ghostty state as a second master value.

3. Persistence
   - Only root `appearance.mode` persists desired active appearance.
   - Mars receives launch environment plus its bounded live control. Zellij receives fresh materialization plus its native live action. Neither adapter writes an active mirror to Mars, Zellij, Yazi, or Ghostty configuration.
   - Component dark/light names remain component preferences, not copies of root state.

4. Fresh and live application
   - Fresh managed launch resolves the root value before starting Mars/Zellij and projects the same value independently to each owner.
   - A writable Ratconfig save persists the validated root value first, then attempts Mars and the current managed Zellij session independently. Results are reported independently as applied, not applicable, or failed.
   - A partial or total live failure never rolls back truthful persisted intent. It remains visible, and the next managed launch converges from the saved root value. No retries, polling, or background synchronizer are added.

5. Unmanaged hosts
   - `yzx launch` applies the terminal half through managed Mars. `yzx enter`, SSH, and no-Mars packages never rewrite or control the ambient host terminal.
   - Managed Zellij still follows root appearance in those sessions. The terminal result is reported as unmanaged/not applicable, not as a failed config save. No OSC inference or host-theme guessing is part of the initial slice.
   - Status/help may explain that the user must configure an unmanaged host separately; entry remains allowed.

6. Component intent
   - Zellij stores independent dark/light theme names. An explicit static packaged or custom `theme` is a fixed override and opts out of root projection while preserving the pair.
   - Resetting the fixed override returns to following and applies the current root-selected pair member to the active managed session when addressable.
   - Yazi and Ghostty do not join the initial implementation.

7. Home Manager
   - Declarative source is `programs.yazelix.config.settings.appearance.mode = "dark" | "light"`. It generates the same root `config.toml`; no separate Home Manager appearance option or mirror is introduced.
   - Ratconfig presents the root row as Home Manager-owned/read-only with existing guidance to edit `programs.yazelix.config.settings` and run the normal Home Manager switch.
   - A Home Manager switch updates persisted declarative intent but does not add an activation hook or mutate a running terminal/session. The new value applies on the next managed launch.

8. Mars inventory interaction
   - Core contains the sole writable/recommended appearance row. Mars Overview omits `mars.appearance.preset`.
   - Mars All may retain the complete native field only as read-only discovery, labeled as standalone-Mars configuration overridden by root appearance in managed Yazelix. Its native-file action remains available and respects existing Home Manager/read-only rules.
   - Complete inventory consumption must not recommend, inline-edit, or theme Ratconfig from the native Mars row.

## Scope

This bead records the contract only. Implementation belongs to the existing root/Mars, Ratconfig, Zellij pair, direct-action, and integration child beads. No source, compatibility alias, protocol, backend, or new Home Manager surface is added here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The matrix covers absent/dark/light/invalid root state; valid/conflicting/invalid native Mars state; fresh/live/partial-failure behavior; fixed/follow Zellij state; unmanaged hosts; and Home Manager ownership without two persisted authorities.
- Every dependent bead names one owner, apply route, persistence boundary, and failure result.
- Mars complete discovery remains truthful without exposing a second writable managed appearance control.
- Auto/system, CSI 2031, Yazi live following, and Ghostty adaptation remain explicit future scope.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop implementation if two persisted values can both claim active managed appearance.
- Stop if a live adapter must rewrite user-owned terminal/application configuration or if one live failure rolls back valid root intent.
- Stop if `yzx enter`, SSH, or `yazelix-no-mars` attempts to control the ambient terminal.
- Stop if Home Manager requires a second appearance option or an activation-time mutation hook.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S, risk LOW, leverage HIGH. Rejected: Mars as global authority, synchronized mirrors, auto in the first slice, CSI 2031 for already-known root state, silently masking invalid native configuration, warning on every valid native conflict, host-theme guessing, all-session process scanning, and a dedicated Home Manager appearance schema.
close_reason: Decision complete: explicit dark/light authority, precedence, persistence, live failure, unmanaged-host, Home Manager, and Mars inventory contracts recorded and handed off.

title: Persist root appearance and apply it to Mars
description:
## Why

Root `appearance.mode` needs one honest projection into Mars without a second live-control protocol. Mars already owns a sparse native field and watches its config directory, so Yazelix can persist the global choice and update only that field.

## User-visible contract

Root `appearance.mode = "dark" | "light"` is the Yazelix appearance authority and Ratconfig palette source. In packages containing Mars, a global save or reset writes only `mars.appearance.preset` in writable `~/.config/yazelix/mars/config.toml`; Mars reloads it through its existing watcher. `yzx launch` performs the same reconciliation, so a direct manual edit can diverge only until the next global save or launch. The native Mars appearance row is hidden from the normal Mars tab.

A store-backed or otherwise read-only Mars file is never changed; the validated root mode is passed as `MARS_APPEARANCE` for the next managed launch. Writable launches remove inherited `MARS_APPEARANCE` so the watched file stays authoritative. `yzx enter` and packages without Mars do not project or create Mars config. If projection fails after a UI save, root intent stays persisted and the error says Mars was not updated.

## Ownership and scope

- `yzx-config` owns root validation, the hidden projection field, safe sparse writes, and Ratconfig integration.
- `yzx launch` owns pre-launch reconciliation and the read-only environment fallback.
- Mars continues to own native parsing, palette behavior, and file watching.
- Preserve every unrelated Mars value and comment supported by the TOML adapter.
- Add no socket, daemon, watcher, compatibility alias, or Mars source change.
- Do not coordinate Zellij, Yazi, or Ghostty in this bead.

## Verification

Focused tests prove root validation and UI authority; hidden native field behavior; preservation of unrelated Mars values; reset to the root default; honest partial failure; no-Mars non-mutation; read-only fallback; strict launch protocol parsing; writable stale-environment removal; Home Manager projection; and packaged contract behavior. Run `cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-config/Cargo.toml`, runtime Rust tests, `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary profile install. Refresh the installed runtime after successful flake verification.

## Rejected alternatives

A Unix socket or other Mars live-control API was rejected as unnecessary protocol surface. Making the native Mars field the global authority was rejected because future Zellij, Yazi, and terminal adapters need one product-level setting. Environment-only projection was rejected for writable config because it cannot change a running Mars process and would override later file reloads.
notes: Implemented the maintainer-selected managed-config projection. Root appearance.mode is validated dark/light, recommended in Core, and used by Ratconfig. Writable Mars config receives only mars.appearance.preset on global save/reset and before yzx launch; read-only/Home Manager Mars files remain unchanged and receive the validated mode through MARS_APPEARANCE on launch. Writable launch removes stale MARS_APPEARANCE. No-Mars and yzx enter paths do not project. Failure preserves root intent and reports partial convergence. Mars yzt-7z5 was retired without source work because the existing watcher supplies live reload. Verification passed: 54 yzx-config tests, 8 runtime tests, nix flake check, all-systems show, full package build, isolated profile install/version, rustfmt, diff check, exact 22,212-line scorecard, and installed profile refresh. No GUI was launched.
close_reason: Completed: root appearance now projects truthfully to writable Mars config, uses launch-only environment fallback for read-only ownership, preserves no-Mars behavior, and passes all focused, Nix, package, and install gates.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Fresh-eyes and isomorphic simplification pass (2026-07-25): fixed reset notices so they retain “Now inheriting” through both writable and read-only Mars outcomes; made partial-projection errors neutral (“Updated”) for both save and reset; changed Mars patching to preserve dangling symlinks on failure and skip atomic rewrites when the requested native value is already identical; collapsed duplicated UI set/reset orchestration; removed an unobservable Runtime mutation; and made the helper protocol parser exact. Added a dangling-symlink regression contract. Verification passed: 55 config tests, 8 runtime tests, clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt, diff check, nix flake check, all-systems evaluation, full package build, isolated profile install, and installed runtime refresh. Net result: 42 fewer production Rust lines, 19 lines of regression coverage, and 21 fewer tracked project lines overall. Rejected broader writable-symlink policy changes because live watcher behavior and cross-owner semantics are not proven; rejected collapsing the explicit config/environment projection states because the UI and launcher consume distinct outcomes.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Second fresh-eyes and simplification pass (2026-07-25): fixed automatic appearance projection replacing a valid symlinked Mars config when the selected mode changed. All symlinked Mars config is now treated as externally managed: Yazelix leaves the link and target untouched and uses the existing MARS_APPEARANCE next-launch fallback. Updated UI feedback and ownership documentation to match. Verification passed: 55 config tests including the valid-symlink regression, 8 runtime tests, clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt, diff check, the full 97-check flake suite, all-systems evaluation, default package build, isolated profile install/version, and installed runtime refresh. Rejected a general Ratconfig symlink policy and in-place target editing because they broaden ownership and cannot guarantee Mars watcher behavior for targets outside its config directory.

title: Move Ratconfig appearance control to Core
description:
## Why

Ratconfig currently treats `mars.appearance.preset` as both terminal configuration and its own UI theme source. Once root Yazelix appearance is authoritative, leaving that Mars row writable would create two controls with conflicting intent and would let the complete-Mars-inventory work reintroduce the conflict later.

## Evidence

- `crates/yzx-config/src/model.rs:213-225` maps the Mars field into `ConfigUiThemeSwitcher`.
- `crates/yzx-config/src/catalog.rs:384-386` describes the row as Mars-specific.
- `crates/yzx-config/src/main.rs:919-935,1315-1323` tests the current Mars-owned UI source.
- Open bead `yazelix-5vl-core-all-config-discovery-lsw.3` recommends and promises discovery of `mars.appearance.preset`.

## User-visible contract

Core presents one appearance choice backed by root Yazelix configuration. Changing it updates Ratconfig immediately and uses the already-implemented terminal adapter for runtime application. The Mars tab does not expose a second writable appearance selector. Ratconfig remains generic and learns no Mars, Zellij, Yazi, or Ghostty synchronization policy.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add the root field to the correct Core catalog/recommendation surface after its runtime adapter exists.
- Move `ConfigUiThemeSwitcher` to the root field.
- Remove or make unavailable the Mars appearance row exactly as decided by the authority bead.
- Reconcile the exception with complete Mars inventory bead `.3` so later catalog consumption cannot silently restore a second control.
- Preserve sparse root intent, reset semantics, Home Manager ownership, Overview/All behavior, and apply status truth.
- Update docs, CHANGELOG, architecture, and README LOC scorecard.

Out of scope:
- No Mars live-control implementation, terminal protocol, theme-pair selection, Ratconfig library change, compatibility alias, or second appearance field.

## Implementation Notes

1. Depend on the working root-to-Mars adapter so every visible save has a truthful effect.
2. Keep backend-native appearance available only through the exact advanced/native-file policy selected by the authority bead.
3. Prefer deleting the old local Mars field policy over adding a hidden alias.
4. Dependency decision: reuse the existing Ratconfig theme-switcher API and root sparse patcher. Add no crate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One model test proves the Core field is the only writable appearance identity and drives dark/light Ratconfig rendering.
- Tests prove save, reset, invalid input, and Home Manager read-only behavior.
- A parity check proves complete Mars inventory cannot expose the excluded/derived selector contrary to the decision.
- `cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-config/Cargo.toml`, `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary profile install should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if both root and Mars appearance remain writable in Ratconfig.
- Stop if hiding the row also makes native Mars configuration unrepairable without the agreed advanced path.
- Stop before changing Ratconfig if its existing host-declared switcher can express the design.
- Stop if the root adapter is not yet truthful for fresh and live behavior.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S/M. Risk MEDIUM because this is an authority cutover. Related open work: `yazelix-5vl-core-all-config-discovery-lsw.3`. Rejected: duplicate controls, visual-only relabeling of a Mars-owned value, and teaching Ratconfig product policy.
notes: Final maintainer contract implemented with .2: root appearance.mode is the sole writable Ratconfig appearance identity and drives the palette immediately. mars.appearance.preset is absent from the Mars tab in both Overview and All; users can still edit the native file manually, but global save or launch reconciles it. The future complete-Mars-inventory bead has an explicit ledger comment requiring this single product-policy exclusion, so catalog parity cannot restore the duplicate control. Tests cover root switcher identity, hidden native field, manual divergence, reset, invalid values, Home Manager/read-only behavior, and no-Mars behavior. Full verification is recorded on .2.
close_reason: Completed with the revised .2 vertical slice: Core owns the sole appearance switch and the duplicate Mars-native row is hidden, with future inventory reconciliation recorded.

title: Select the packaged Zellij dark/light theme pair
description: Select the inherited Zellij theme pair from the exact pinned inventory. Maintainer dogfood selected `gruvbox-light` for light appearance. The dark member was subsequently revised from `gruvbox-dark` to `ansi`: the maintainer dislikes `gruvbox-dark`, `default` is only a fallback and cannot resolve as a native pair name, while `ansi` is an actual bundled theme. Final inherited pair: `theme_dark = ansi`, `theme_light = gruvbox-light`. Yazelix owns only these names; Zellij owns palettes. Users may replace either member with any packaged or preserved custom name.
acceptance_criteria: Both selected names exist in the pinned theme inventory. The light member has maintainer visual approval. The dark member is a resolvable native theme rather than the non-name `default`. Pair fields retain packaged and custom alternatives. No palette copy, classifier, registry, alias, or Zellij fork change is introduced.
notes: Final decision supersedes the original same-family Gruvbox pair. Rejected gruvbox-dark by maintainer preference. Rejected default because native theme_dark resolution requires a real theme name. Rejected separate curated light/dark pools and name heuristics because the pinned and custom inventories have no reliable hue metadata. The pair-only model also supersedes the earlier static fixed-override concept.
close_reason: Decision complete: selected packaged gruvbox-dark/gruvbox-light pair from maintainer dogfood and pinned-source inspection; alternatives and final integration verification recorded.

title: Expose paired Zellij dark and light themes
description: Expose the native Zellij theme_dark and theme_light pair through Yazelix and Ratconfig. Yazelix owns inherited defaults of ansi for dark appearance and gruvbox-light for light appearance. Both fields use the same pinned packaged-theme inventory and preserve custom native names. The legacy static theme field is no longer a competing managed setting: preserve it in the user sidecar, diagnose it as ignored, and omit it from the materialized runtime config. This bead owns configuration and materialization only; the dependent live adapter applies root appearance to active sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Ratconfig exposes Dark theme and Light theme with inherited ansi and gruvbox-light values; both offer the pinned packaged inventory and retain custom names. Saves and resets remain sparse, invalid fields are localized, and Home Manager ownership stays read-only. The packaged runtime always contains a complete native pair. A legacy static theme assignment remains untouched on disk, is reported as ignored, and is absent from materialized runtime configuration. No active-theme selector or live Zellij action is added. Focused Rust and Nix contract checks pass, documentation and LOC scorecard are current.
notes: Implemented the pair-only model agreed on 2026-07-25. Ratconfig exposes Dark theme and Light theme with one shared 41-theme pool; custom names discovered on either pair member are available to both. Inherited defaults are ansi and gruvbox-light. Sparse save/reset, field-local invalid state, watched-config refresh, and Home Manager refusal remain intact. Legacy static `theme` assignments are preserved in the user sidecar, diagnosed as ignored, and omitted from generated runtime configuration. An explicit sidecar pair member replaces only its matching packaged default, leaving the native pair complete. The fresh-eyes pass fixed a materialization scanner bug where a brace in a leading hash comment could hide later top-level fields, corrected the stale detailed LOC total, inlined a single-use diagnostic wrapper, and consolidated repetitive test assertions; the resulting Rust surface is six lines smaller. Verification passed: 55 Rust tests, strict Clippy, rustfmt, diff hygiene, full `nix flake check`, all-system flake show, Yazelix package build, isolated profile install, and installed profile refresh. No GUI dogfood was run because this bead changes configuration/materialization rather than the live root action owned by `.7`.
close_reason: Implemented and fully verified the pair-only Zellij dark/light configuration and materialization contract

title: Prove the live root-to-Mars-and-Zellij appearance chain
description: Prove that one Core dark/light control produces a readable matching Mars and Zellij presentation on fresh launch and live dark-to-light-to-dark changes. This is the narrow composed-runtime gate after owner-level beads: root persistence, Mars projection, Zellij paired themes, native current-session actions, plugins, transparency, Home Manager, and truthful partial failure. title: Make initial and live bar palette rendering structurally complete
description:
## Why

The Yazelix bar correctly uses one runtime template with dark and light internal palettes, but initial rendering and live host-theme overlays enumerate theme-sensitive output through different paths. A future bar field can therefore be added to launch rendering without being added to live switching, or vice versa. One semantic field contract should prove both modes remain complete without exposing presets or configuration.

## Evidence

- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-bar/src/appearance.rs:49`: `BarStyle` is the component-owned dark/light palette and `template_replacements` covers only template placeholders.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:1553`: `runtime_host_theme_fields` separately enumerates the fields replaced by live mode overlays.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:3914`: current runtime tests sample individual initial and overlay literals but do not prove complete field parity.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/zjstatus/src/config.rs:62`: zjstatus generically overlays any selected `host_theme_dark_` or `host_theme_light_` key, so completeness belongs in bar rendering rather than zjstatus policy.

## Scope

In scope:
- The child-owned Yazelix runtime renderer in `yazelix-zellij-bar/src/appearance.rs` and `src/lib.rs`.
- One strong contract test that proves every theme-sensitive initial field has the corresponding dark and light live representation and that selecting either overlay reproduces the intended mode rendering.
- The smallest refactor needed to make the field set structurally shared if the contract cannot be expressed cleanly against the current shape.
- Updating the pinned child revision and Yazelix scorecard or documentation only when the child implementation changes the consumed package surface.

Out of scope:
- New user-facing presets, settings, palette registries, or automatic color classification.
- Changing the chosen colors or the ansi and gruvbox-light Zellij defaults.
- Replacing the paired palettes with one fixed or terminal-dependent palette.
- A generic cross-component theme bus.
- Reworking zjstatus widget lifecycle unless the parity contract exposes a confirmed generic defect.

## Implementation Notes

1. Model the theme-sensitive runtime fields once, or derive a complete semantic comparison from the existing renderer without copying another key list into the test.
2. Generate or validate initial dark, initial light, live dark, and live light output through that shared contract.
3. Keep one public runtime template and two child-owned internal palettes; do not introduce separate bar presets.
4. Prefer deleting duplicated field assembly over adding an adapter abstraction.
5. If the child revision changes, pin the exact verified revision in Yazelix and update required LOC and changelog surfaces.

## Verification

- In `yazelix-zellij-bar`, `cargo test` should exit 0 and the parity contract should cover the complete theme-sensitive field set for both modes.
- In `yazelix-zellij-bar`, `cargo build --release` should exit 0.
- In `yazelix-zellij-bar`, `nix build .#yazelix_zellij_bar --no-link` should exit 0.
- If Yazelix pins a new child revision, `nix flake check` and `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` should exit 0 from the Yazelix repository.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the cited rendering paths have already converged on one structural field contract.
- Stop if completion requires a user-facing preset or a generic appearance framework.
- Stop if a failure is actually owned by generic zjstatus overlay semantics; create or update a narrowly scoped owner-repository bead instead of absorbing that work.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S, risk LOW, confidence HIGH. The desired model remains one bar template with two internal palettes. Rejected: one fixed hex palette because it cannot preserve contrast on dark and light transparent backgrounds; one ANSI-only palette because it makes the integrated product appearance terminal-dependent; separate public presets because they create synchronization and configuration state.
notes:
Implemented and published in Yazelix Zellij Bar commits `ed204673e73f54b372c0eafb71eb4f9b23f0f8cd` and `92258bbae0362f0d558193d6d85b2ed7728718c4`; Yazelix pins the final revision. One `runtime_theme_fields` result per palette now drives both active launch assignments and prefixed live overlays. The runtime template has one active-theme block, the old placeholder replacement path and three dead mode styles were deleted, and the selected four-file surface is 52 lines smaller. A contract test proves unique keys, identical dark/light key coverage, and active-to-live value parity for both modes without a copied expected key list. Before/after CLI snapshots retained the same 93 assignment keys and values in dark and light.

The first integrated check found that Yazelix layout validation intentionally consumes the active `format_right` trailing `// {datetime}` marker. The final shared serializer preserves that integration marker without restoring a second field owner. Final verification passed: 56 child Rust tests, rustfmt, release build, exact clean-revision child Nix build, exact remote pin assertion, final `nix flake check` with 77 checks, all-system flake show, Yazelix package build, temporary-profile install, diff hygiene, and installed-profile refresh. Strict host Rust 1.96 Clippy was already red before editing and remains red with exactly the same four unrelated findings (`derivable_impls` and three `manual_is_multiple_of`); no new lint appeared. Pre-existing child README, flake, and untracked preset work was preserved. No zjstatus lifecycle work was created because no state-loss or rerun defect was reproduced.

title: Audit and retire stale Yazelix worktrees
description:
## Why

Yazelix currently registers three secondary worktrees in addition to the primary checkout. They include one known disposable repin worktree, one worktree whose `.git` file points at a moved/nonexistent administrative directory, and one clean but historically divergent audit branch. Blind deletion could discard untracked files or branch-only work, while leaving all of them indefinitely creates workspace and branch ambiguity.

## Evidence

- `git worktree list --porcelain` on 2026-07-16 listed the primary checkout plus `yazelix_light_mode`, `yazelix_rust_loc_audit`, and detached `yazelix-mars-repin-20260716`.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix` is the primary `main` checkout at `79a18c0a`, two commits behind `origin/main`, with unrelated tracked modifications. It must not be deleted or reset as part of this cleanup.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix-mars-repin-20260716` is detached at `dc197a1a`, clean, fully contained in `origin/main`, and was created only for the Mars repin transaction.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/worktrees/yazelix_light_mode/.git` points to nonexistent `/home/lucca/pjs/yazelix/.git/worktrees/yazelix_light_mode`, so ordinary `git -C ... status` fails. Its branch tip is `67371615` (`feat: add yzxterm appearance handling`), it has no remote branch, and it has no merge base with current `origin/main`.
- `/home/lucca/pjs/worktrees/yazelix_rust_loc_audit` is clean at `b05ea629` (`Refresh Rust LOC ownership audit`), has no remote branch, and has no merge base with current `origin/main`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Inventory every registered Yazelix worktree, its administrative metadata, status, branch/ref, remote publication, reachability, and unique work.
- Treat all secondary worktrees as removal candidates, but preserve any dirty, untracked, or still-useful branch-only work before removal.
- Repair the stale `yazelix_light_mode` worktree pointer temporarily if needed to obtain a trustworthy status, or make a filesystem-level backup before any manual cleanup.
- Decide whether the two old branch tips contain anything worth porting to current Nova; preserve selected work as explicit beads/commits rather than keeping ambiguous worktrees indefinitely.
- Remove safe secondary worktrees with `git worktree remove`, then prune stale administrative entries and optionally delete obsolete local branches only after their tips are preserved or explicitly rejected.
- Leave the primary checkout and its current uncommitted changes intact; after secondary cleanup, report how its local `main` should be advanced safely.

Out of scope:
- Do not reset, clean, stash, commit, or delete files from the primary dirty checkout without separate maintainer approval.
- Do not force-delete an uninspectable or unmerged worktree merely to reduce the count.
- Do not port light-mode or Rust-audit code in this bead; create focused follow-ups for anything deliberately retained.
- Do not delete remote branches or rewrite repository history.

## Implementation Notes

1. Fetch `origin/main` and capture `git worktree list --porcelain`, `git branch -vv`, and `git worktree prune --dry-run --verbose`.
2. For every secondary path, record `git status --porcelain=v1`, HEAD, branch, upstream, remote branch existence, and reachability from `origin/main`.
3. For `yazelix_light_mode`, first preserve the directory, then use `git worktree repair` or the main repository metadata to restore inspection. If status still cannot be trusted, stop before deletion and present the backup/recovery choice.
4. For branch-only histories with no merge base, inspect the tip tree and a bounded set of relevant commits rather than assuming thousands of historical commits are intentional unique work.
5. Remove only worktrees classified as clean and disposable, using normal `git worktree remove`; use `--force` only with explicit maintainer approval after preservation evidence.
6. Run `git worktree prune`, verify the final list, and record retained branches/worktrees and their reasons.

## Verification

- `git worktree list --porcelain` should show only the primary checkout plus any explicitly retained worktrees.
- `git worktree prune --dry-run --verbose` should report no stale administrative entries after cleanup.
- `git status --porcelain=v1` in the primary checkout should show the same pre-existing user changes; cleanup must not alter them.
- Every removed branch tip must either be reachable from a retained ref, recorded in an explicit backup ref, or documented as intentionally discarded with maintainer approval.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before deletion if a worktree is dirty, contains untracked files, cannot be inspected reliably, or has useful work not preserved elsewhere.
- Stop before deleting any local branch whose tip is not reachable from a retained ref unless the maintainer explicitly rejects that work.
- Stop if repairing worktree metadata would overwrite the primary checkout metadata or working files.

## Maintenance Notes

- Effort: S-M. Risk: MED because two old branches are unrelated to current Nova history. Confidence: HIGH that the temporary repin worktree is disposable; LOW until inspection for the stale light-mode directory; MED for retiring the Rust LOC audit worktree.
- Rejected alternative: delete every secondary directory immediately. Worktree count is less important than preserving unmerged or untracked work.
- Prefer a final state with one authoritative primary checkout and short-lived task worktrees that are removed after their commits are published.
close_reason: Removed all three secondary worktrees: detached Mars repin, clean Rust LOC audit, and repaired/forced stale light-mode. Preserved local branch refs yazelix_light_mode at 67371615 and yazelix_rust_loc_audit at b05ea629, so committed history remains recoverable. Explicit maintainer stale designation authorized discarding the light-mode worktree's sole uncommitted change: the obsolete in-progress Restore Linux Foot terminal variant planning line. Primary dirty checkout was not reset or otherwise altered. Final worktree list contains only the primary checkout and prune dry-run is empty.

title: Document macOS XDG opt-in and declarative config source reuse
description:
## Why

A macOS Home Manager or nix-darwin user may prefer Linux-style XDG locations and one declarative source for configuration used both inside and outside Yazelix. Nova intentionally keeps its managed runtime under a Yazelix-owned namespaced tree and does not adopt ambient Helix, Yazi, Zellij, terminal, Starship, or shell files automatically. The supported answer needs concise documentation rather than another runtime integration mode.

## Outcome

Document two independent opt-in patterns:

1. How macOS users can deliberately export Linux-style XDG base directories through their own Home Manager or nix-darwin launchd configuration so GUI-launched and shell-launched tools see a consistent environment.
2. How Home Manager users can reuse the same source files for a normal host tool and the corresponding programs.yazelix.config native text/source option while installing them at separate owned destinations.

State clearly that XDG_CONFIG_HOME changes the base directory but Yazelix still uses its own yazelix subdirectory, and that declarative source reuse is not ambient-config adoption.

## Scope

- Provide one concise, current Home Manager or nix-darwin example for propagating appropriate XDG variables on macOS.
- Avoid prescribing an unsafe persistent XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; explain its lifecycle requirements or omit it from the general example.
- Provide representative shared-source examples for a safe native file such as Helix languages.toml or a Yazi override.
- Explain which Yazelix integration-owned configuration cannot be replaced wholesale, especially managed Zellij nodes and required Yazi or Helix bindings.
- Link the canonical Nova Home Manager text/source options and ownership diagnostics.
- Keep the documentation platform-aware and use public Yazelix Nova names after canonical cutover.

## Guardrails

- Add no runtime setting, global launchctl mutation, ambient-config reader, import side effect, or compatibility mode.
- Do not tell Yazelix to move, overwrite, or take ownership of native tool configuration.
- Do not imply that setting XDG_CONFIG_HOME makes ambient tool files control the managed runtime.

## Verification

- The documented Nix example evaluates on the intended macOS Home Manager or nix-darwin surface, or the untestable platform gap is stated explicitly.
- Paths and option names match the canonical Nova Home Manager module.
- The shared-source example installs the same immutable source at two explicit destinations without duplicate file content.
- Documentation clearly distinguishes XDG base selection, Yazelix namespacing, declarative source reuse, and ambient configuration.

title: Adopt Mars localhost and URL link-detection fix
description:
## Why

The Yazelix runtime packages Mars as its terminal, and current dogfooding reports that some printed links remain non-clickable, with localhost-style URLs suspected. Mars bead `yzt-harden-localhost-url-link-detection-5jw` owns reproduction, regex and hit-span tests, and the terminal fix. - Owning bead: `yzt-harden-localhost-url-link-detection-5jw`
- Previous completed Mars feature: `yzt-t6w7.2`

## User-visible contract

In the packaged Yazelix runtime, URLs printed by development servers and ordinary terminal tools are fully clickable through the existing Mars gesture. Out of scope:

- Changing Zellij mouse policy, keybindings, desktop openers, Home Manager scope, or unrelated Mars settings.
- Expanding link behavior beyond the contract chosen and tested by the Mars owner bead.
- Updating the lock before the Mars revision is published and verified.

## Implementation Notes

2. Review the Mars commit, scorecard entry, focused regex tests, false-positive cases, and manual standalone evidence.
3. Update the locked Mars input without unrelated lock churn.
4. Refresh the installed Yazelix runtime only after the flake and package checks pass.
5. Dogfood the exact failing strings inside the packaged `yzx` workspace.

## Verification

- The owning Mars bead is closed with a published revision and recorded focused/full test evidence.
- `nix flake check` exits 0.
- `nix flake show --all-systems` evaluates the advertised outputs.
- `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` exits 0.
- `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` installs successfully.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the failing string works in standalone Mars but not through Yazelix; capture Zellij input and opener evidence before changing either repo.
- Stop if adoption requires main-repository link parsing, regex tests, or mouse-policy duplication.
- Stop before unrelated flake-lock, runtime, Home Manager, or configuration changes.

## Maintenance Notes

Owner split: Mars owns detection, extraction, click hit spans, and regression tests; Yazelix owns the locked child revision and packaged-runtime proof.

Effort: XS after the Mars fix. Risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH in the ownership split.

title: Add a persistent per-tab Yazi workspace popup
description:
## Why

The managed sidebar is useful as a compact editor companion, but it is not a comfortable full-screen browser for exploratory navigation. Yazelix needs one persistent Yazi popup before global zoxide and workspace-selection behavior can be designed without treating Yazi as a one-shot fzf wrapper.

## User-visible contract

- `Alt Shift Y` toggles one managed Yazi popup in the active tab from any unlocked focus state.
- The popup launches at the orchestrator-owned canonical workspace root.
- Toggling or displacing the popup hides it instead of terminating it. Reopening at the same canonical root preserves the live Yazi process, cwd, cursor, and in-memory navigation state.
- If the canonical root changes while the popup is hidden, the existing popup lifecycle may discard the stale process and launch a fresh Yazi at the new requested root.
- The popup uses the same managed Yazi package, layered user configuration, themes, plugins, preview tools, and ordinary editor opener as the sidebar.
- The popup has an explicit workspace-popup role and never registers itself as the managed sidebar. Popup navigation must not replace sidebar identity, move the tiled sidebar, or redefine the tab workspace.
- Ordinary file opens retain the existing `yzx-open` contract: requested targets reach the editor while ordinary navigation does not retarget the canonical workspace.

## Scope

- Add one packaged `yazi` popup specification using the existing popup plugin and pane orchestrator.
- Add the fixed, documented `Alt Shift Y` key and reserve the packaged popup id/title and key collision.
- Reuse the existing `yzx-yazi` launcher with the smallest private role marker needed to omit sidebar-only registration and presentation behavior.
- Use the existing hide-on-toggle lifecycle; do not add disk persistence or a second state store.
- Update current-state docs, changelog, key inventory, generated-config contract, and README LOC scorecard.

## Out of scope

- Moving global `Alt z`, launching zoxide automatically, choosing a workspace commit key, retargeting, or resynchronizing the sidebar after a commit. The dependent Alt-z bead owns that workflow.
- A configurable Yazi-popup key, general popup settings, multiple Yazi popup roles, general file picking, search, layout redesign, or sidebar hide-on-open behavior.
- Child-repository changes unless a focused failing contract proves the existing generic popup/orchestrator capabilities insufficient.

## Verification

- Generated config contains one hide-policy Yazi popup launched through the managed Yazi role at canonical workspace cwd and one global `Alt Shift Y` orchestrator binding.
- The popup id/title and key cannot be shadowed by a custom popup.
- The popup role does not register `YAZI_ID` as sidebar state; the ordinary tiled Yazi still does.
- Existing sidebar `Alt z`, ordinary Yazi opens, sidebar registration, and all other popup lifecycles remain unchanged.
- Focused Rust and contract checks, `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a clean temporary-profile install pass.
- Manual dogfood, when explicitly requested, verifies hide/show state preservation from editor, shell, sidebar, and sidebar-hidden focus states.

## Rejected alternatives

A one-shot Yazi process that immediately runs fzf and exits was rejected because it prevents navigation and uses Yazi only as a wrapper. Reusing the tiled sidebar was rejected because workspace browsing should not require sidebar focus or mutate sidebar-local state.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed global `Alt Shift Y` toggles one per-tab managed Yazi popup at the canonical workspace root. The popup uses the existing managed Yazi configuration and hide lifecycle, preserves live navigation state while the root is unchanged, restarts when its requested canonical root becomes stale, and cannot register as or mutate the tiled sidebar. Ordinary navigation and opens retain existing workspace semantics. This bead does not change `Alt z`, launch zoxide, or add a workspace commit action.
notes: Implemented the first split slice only. Alt Shift Y now toggles one per-tab managed Yazi popup through the pane orchestrator at the canonical workspace root. The packaged popup uses hide-on-toggle persistence and the existing managed Yazi launcher/config/opener. A private workspace-popup role prevents sidebar-state and sidebar-status registration, so popup navigation does not replace or move the tiled sidebar. Existing sidebar Alt z remains unchanged for the dependent bead. Verification passed: focused launcher tests (2), yzx-tutor tests (12), pinned yzx-config tests (48), pinned materialization/contracts builds, nix flake check, nix flake show --all-systems, nix build .#yazelix, temporary-profile installation, crate-specific rustfmt checks, git diff --check, and nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix. GUI dogfood was not launched because repository instructions require an explicit request.
close_reason: Persistent per-tab Yazi popup implemented and verified; Alt-z intentionally remains in the dependent bead.

title: Report Classic migration residue in yzx doctor
description: Add a read-only Classic-residue diagnostic to yzx doctor. Scan only the active Nova config and state roots. Report recognized Classic artifacts with their exact paths, whether Nova uses them, and whether ownership is certain or ambiguous. Never follow symlinks, never mutate, and keep residue as warnings rather than a doctor failure. Do not report current Nova yazi, zellij, helix, helix-steel, or logs state. Warn that external scripts may still reference residue. Extend the existing Classic-to-Nova README guidance. Owner: runtime/yzx/doctor.rs. Sources of truth: v17.12 generated-state contracts plus Nova paths/runtime owners. Rejected from this slice: archive or cleanup commands, automatic startup/activation work, active-session discovery, executing Classic state, compatibility aliases, public JSON/status schema changes, and classic/classic-bridge branch governance.
design: Keep detection in runtime/yzx/doctor.rs. Scan only active config/state roots. Treat configs/ and sessions/ as ambiguous because their contents are not provably Classic-owned; treat the exact regular Classic Nushell extern and fingerprint paths as certain; treat known backup filename matches and every final symlink as ambiguous. Walk fixed state paths one component at a time with symlink_metadata and stop at symlinked parents. Residue is informational and never changes doctor success. No archive command: Classic has no ownership manifest that makes whole-tree archival safe, and relevant live-session discovery is not a reliable cleanup guard.

When recognized Classic roots or migration files exist, it prints one warning per exact path with nova=unused and ownership=certain or ownership=ambiguous, followed by the external-consumer warning. Symlinks are never followed and are always ambiguous. Current Nova yazi, zellij, helix, helix-steel, and logs paths are never reported. Residue does not change the successful doctor exit status and no file is created, moved, deleted, or rewritten by the scanner.
