title: Publish Nova aarch64-darwin outputs to Cachix
description:
## Why

GitHub issue #666 identified that Nova's main-branch cache workflow publishes only x86_64-linux. The existing Darwin smoke and version-gate jobs build the canonical aarch64-darwin full package, runtime package, and Home Manager check, but do not configure Cachix, so those store paths remain unavailable from yazelix.cachix.org.

## Contract

On canonical main-branch pushes and manual dispatch, a guarded macos-15 job publishes packages.aarch64-darwin.yazelix, packages.aarch64-darwin.runtime, and checks.aarch64-darwin.home_manager through the existing Yazelix Cachix cache. Missing credentials skip publishing clearly. Successful runs verify that each top-level output has a reachable narinfo. Existing Darwin smoke and version-gate ownership remains unchanged.

## Scope

- Extend the existing Publish Nix Cache workflow rather than creating another workflow.
- Follow Nova's current token guard, canonical-repository guard, Nix installer, resource limits, and Cachix action versions.
- Configure the Cachix client/auth through the action but disable its asynchronous post-job push; synchronously `cachix push` the three returned paths before probing them.
- Build without modifying flake.lock and retain useful build logs.
- Probe the narinfo for every returned top-level aarch64-darwin output with bounded retries for cache propagation.
- Keep desktop-entry and runtime behavior checks in the existing Darwin workflows.
- Update current-state documentation/scorecard required by repository policy.

## Guardrails

- Do not copy obsolete Classic package names.
- Do not alter package outputs, Home Manager behavior, release commands, or Cachix trust configuration.
- Do not weaken Linux cache publishing or merge unrelated Darwin validation changes.
- Do not require the secret for forks; report a clear skipped publish.

## Verification

Validate workflow syntax/structure locally, exercise repository contract checks, evaluate flake outputs, and run the cheapest exact Nix check that covers workflow files and advertised outputs. Live cache publication and HTTP 200 evidence complete on the first canonical workflow run.
acceptance_criteria: The Publish Nix Cache workflow has a canonical-repository-only macos-15 job guarded by CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN. It installs Nix with bounded resources, configures cachix/cachix-action@v17 for authenticated cache access without an asynchronous post-job push, and builds packages.aarch64-darwin.yazelix, packages.aarch64-darwin.runtime, and checks.aarch64-darwin.home_manager with --no-write-lock-file and build logs. Exactly three returned top-level store paths are pushed synchronously and then checked at yazelix.cachix.org by its narinfo hash with bounded retries. Existing Linux publishing, Darwin smoke, version-gate, and desktop-entry checks remain intact. Focused workflow/contracts checks and flake evaluation pass; a canonical main/manual run provides final publication evidence.
notes: Fresh-eyes review: keep the existing Linux Cachix action unchanged. The Darwin action alone sets skipPush so its explicit cachix push completes before narinfo probes; a misplaced skipPush on Linux was corrected before handoff. Rejected a matrix job, YAML anchors, and a local shared action: they save repeated setup text but obscure the different Linux daemon-push and Darwin synchronous-push lifecycles, change job identity, or add another owner without locally runnable end-to-end proof. The final shell keeps the exact three-path guard and HTTP 200 checks; only redundant formatting and an upstream-impossible empty-line branch were removed.
close_reason: Completed and verified working

title: Restore the Yazi popup on the first toggle after opening a file
description:
## Why

Opening a file from the persistent Yazi popup correctly focuses Helix and removes the popup from view, but `Alt Shift Y` then performs an invisible hide before it can show Yazi again. The user must press the toggle twice. A hide-mode popup must preserve its process state and return on the first toggle whenever the floating layer is already hidden.

## Evidence

- Manual dogfooding on 2026-07-18: selecting a file in the full Yazi popup focuses Helix; the next `Alt Shift Y` appears to do nothing, and a second press restores Yazi.
- `defaults/zellij/config.kdl:49-55` configures Yazi as a persistent `toggle_close_behavior "hide"` popup; lines 102-107 route its key through the orchestrator to `yzpp`.
- `crates/yzx-open/src/main.rs:331-346` explicitly focuses the live Helix pane before sending the bridge request.
- `../yazelix-zellij-popup/src/main.rs:39-43,78-85` caches active-tab position and viewport but drops `TabInfo.are_floating_panes_visible`.
- `../yazelix-zellij-popup/src/popup_contract.rs:579-586` treats any matching pane whose pane snapshot is focused as `ToggleFocused`, without knowing whether Zellij has hidden the tab-wide floating layer.
- `../yazelix-zellij/zellij-utils/src/data.rs:2235-2251` and `zellij-server/src/screen.rs:3160-3168` prove that the pinned Zellij contract publishes the missing tab-wide visibility fact.

## User-visible contract

After a successful file open moves focus from the persistent Yazi popup to Helix, one press of `Alt Shift Y` shows and focuses the same live Yazi process. When the floating layer is actually visible and Yazi is focused, one press still hides it. Navigation state and popup launch cwd remain intact.

## Ownership

`yzpp` remains the sole owner of popup lifecycle decisions. The opener and pane orchestrator must not infer or duplicate hide/show state.

## Scope

In scope:
- Teach the popup child toggle resolver about the active tabs `are_floating_panes_visible` fact.
- Treat an existing matching popup as focus/show when the tab-wide floating layer is hidden, even if its pane snapshot still reports focused.
- Preserve the existing focused-visible hide/close policy, suppressed-pane reuse, cwd restart policy, geometry, hooks, and other configured popups.
- Publish the popup child before updating the main flake lock.
- Update the popup README contract, main CHANGELOG, and README LOC scorecard.

Out of scope:
- Changes to Yazi opener behavior, Helix bridge semantics, sidebar hide-on-open policy, popup keybindings, arbitrary delays/retries, or a Yazelix-specific branch in the generic popup plugin.
- Hiding all floating panes from `yzx-open` or adding a second popup state cache.

## Implementation Notes

1. Extend the popup childs active-tab snapshot with the tab-wide floating visibility bit already delivered by `TabUpdate`.
2. Add the smallest pure resolver input needed to distinguish focused-and-visible from focused-but-globally-hidden.
3. For a matching live pane while floating panes are globally hidden, resolve to the existing focus/show path. Keep `ToggleFocused` only for a focused popup on a visible floating layer.
4. Add one regression matrix covering visible focused, visible unfocused, globally hidden focused, suppressed, and missing matching panes. Merge it into the existing toggle contract rather than adding mirror tests.
5. Add no crate, package, timer, polling loop, or compatibility shim.

## Verification

- In `../yazelix-zellij-popup`: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --lib`, `cargo build --target wasm32-wasip1 --profile release`, and `nix build .#yazelix_zellij_popup --no-link` should exit 0.
- The focused child regression should prove that global floating visibility overrides stale pane focus only for the toggle decision.
- After publishing and locking the child: `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` should succeed.
- Upgrade the installed runtime with `nix profile upgrade --refresh yazelix`.
- Manual dogfooding: open Yazi, navigate away from the workspace root, open a file into an existing Helix pane, then press `Alt Shift Y` once. The same Yazi process should reappear at its preserved location. Repeat with an ordinary focused hide and with another configured popup.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and capture the `TabUpdate` and `PaneUpdate` state transition if the reported sequence does not produce `are_floating_panes_visible = false` with a still-focused matching pane; do not compensate with sleeps or retries.
- Stop before changing `yzx-open`, the Helix bridge, the pane orchestrator, or the Zellij fork unless a focused trace disproves the child-owned visibility fix.
- Stop if the resolver would hide or close unrelated user floating panes.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort: S. Risk: LOW/MED because the pure decision is small but the proof crosses Zellij tab and pane state. Confidence: HIGH in the defect and available visibility fact; MED/HIGH in the exact event sequence until the regression trace is captured.

Rejected alternatives: send a blind second toggle, hide all floating panes from the opener, couple Yazi role state into `yzx-open`, cache an independent visible flag, or add timing around focus events.
notes: Implemented in published popup child revision f28d04c3569640acf7cae4c87e56bc6f32ebeaf2. yzpp now carries TabInfo.are_floating_panes_visible into its pure toggle resolver: a matching pane with a stale focused bit resolves to Focus when the tab-wide floating layer is hidden, while a visible focused popup retains its configured hide or close behavior. The regression matrix covers visible focused, hidden-layer focused, visible unfocused, suppressed, and missing panes. Child verification passed: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test --lib (32 tests); cargo build --target wasm32-wasip1 --profile release; nix build .#yazelix_zellij_popup --no-link. Main verification passed: nix flake check; nix flake show --all-systems; nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs; clean temporary-profile install. The installed yazelix profile was refreshed. No GUI session was launched; post-fix manual confirmation remains available in the users next fresh session.
close_reason: Fixed in published yzpp f28d04c and locked into the verified, refreshed Yazelix runtime

title: Allow any managed Yazelix action to be left unmapped
description:
## Why

Managed Yazelix actions currently require a valid key chord. Remapping avoids a particular collision but still forces every packaged action to occupy a chord, even when a user prefers command/menu access or does not use that action. Adding a screen-only escape hatch would create an inconsistent schema, so unmapping should be designed once for the complete managed-key family.

## User-visible contract

A user can explicitly leave any managed Yazelix keybinding unmapped. Omitting a setting still selects its packaged default. An unmapped action produces no Zellij bind, consumes no chord during collision validation, and remains available through any independent command or menu entry it already owns. Other configured and default bindings behave unchanged and apply on the next Yazelix launch.

## Decision work

Choose one clear TOML representation that Ratconfig can edit and that cannot be mistaken for a key chord. Evaluate at least: a string-or-false value such as screen = false, a separate disabled action list, and per-action key/enabled tables. Prefer the smallest representation that works uniformly for every entry in the canonical managed-key inventory. Do not use an empty string, magic chord, or action-specific exception.

## Ownership and scope

Yazelix owns the canonical managed-key schema, validation, runtime config materialization, status text, and key-reference/config-UI presentation. Apply the chosen representation to all managed Yazelix actions together. Keep custom popup key requirements, native Zellij bindings, commands, popup lifecycle, and child repositories unchanged unless the chosen general contract demonstrably requires otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every canonical managed action supports the same explicit unmapped representation.
- Missing values retain packaged defaults; explicit unmapped values do not silently fall back.
- Runtime-generated config removes exactly the disabled bind without malformed KDL or marker leakage.
- Collision validation ignores unmapped actions and still detects duplicates among active managed and custom-popup chords.
- Status and Ratconfig distinguish defaulted, remapped, and unmapped states clearly.
- Documentation states that unmapping removes only the shortcut, not the underlying command/menu capability.
- Focused config tests and generated-runtime contracts cover one disabled popup action, one disabled non-popup action, mixed remapped/unmapped values, and restoration to defaults.

## Out of scope

- Per-mode Zellij binding objects, multiple chords per action, arbitrary raw KDL, disabling native Zellij defaults, changing popup behavior, or making custom popups keyless.

## Verification

Run the yzx-config tests, runtime unit tests, generated contract checks, nix flake check, package build, and temporary-profile install. Do not launch a GUI session unless explicitly requested.

## Maintenance notes

Effort: M. Risk: MED because the value type crosses TOML parsing, Ratconfig editing, validation, status, and KDL materialization. Record the chosen representation and rejected alternatives before implementation.
notes: Decision: use one uniform string-or-false leaf for every managed action (for example, screen = false). Missing remains inherited/default; a string remains an active chord; false means explicitly unmapped. Ratconfig is an owned dependency and gained a project-neutral optional-string capability with a host-supplied disabled label, so Yazelix edits chords as unquoted text and displays false as Unmapped. Rejected a separate disabled-actions list because it creates a second owner; rejected per-action key/enabled tables because they add schema without behavior; rejected empty strings, magic chords, and action-specific exceptions because they blur validation or make the family inconsistent. Implemented all seven managed actions uniformly: config reads preserve false, collision validation skips unmapped actions, generated KDL omits exactly the disabled bind, and status/doctor distinguish default, remapped, and unmapped states. Fresh-eyes follow-up found that the original substring marker could also match an unrelated unbind for the same chord. A focused regression failed before the fix; marking the exact packaged bind preserves the unbind and the generated contract now runs Zellij setup --check on disabled KDL. The stale string-kind managed-key validation branch was deleted. Ratconfig optional-string rendering now has one shared output path at e6ec2ebfe84b2358186410680cbcaf0564eb59a2, which Yazelix pins. Rejected collapsing the two-phase marker pass because it is required for chord swaps; rejected deleting the brace-aware remover because compact and multiline KDL share the contract; rejected folding OptionalString into FreeText or Choice because that loses exact sentinel semantics or adds an option bag. Verification passed: Ratconfig fmt, 123 default tests, 85 no-default tests, 128 all-feature tests, and Clippy; 9 runtime unit tests; generated contracts including native Zellij parsing; all 72 flake checks; flake show; package build; temporary-profile install; and installed-profile refresh. No GUI session was launched, per scope.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes regression fix and simplification pass completed; exact bind omission, native KDL parsing, Ratconfig deduplication, and release checks all verified.

title: Improve Ratconfig light-mode contrast
description:
## Why

Several Ratconfig elements are difficult to read in light appearance because foreground, border, status, and selection colors do not consistently contrast with the light background. The config UI should remain legible without users having to switch Mars back to dark mode.

## Evidence

- Runtime dogfooding report on 2026-07-14: some config-popup elements often have poor contrast in light mode.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:34-59` defines one `ConfigUiThemePalette`, but the light palette still uses named terminal colors such as `Color::Gray` for borders.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:1088-1121` remaps only a fixed set of named colors; every unmatched color passes through unchanged, while many renderer call sites still use hard-coded named colors.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:1656-1667` only proves that plain text and the selected background are not white. It does not defend readable semantic roles or selected-row combinations.

## Scope

### In scope

- Reproduce and list the concrete low-contrast elements in Ratconfig under Mars light appearance, including normal rows, selected rows, borders, metadata, status/error text, and detail/help text.
- Keep Ratconfig's centralized light/dark palette as the single owner and route the failing elements through semantic palette roles.
- Choose light-mode colors that remain distinguishable on both the panel background and selection background.
- Preserve dark-mode behavior unless a shared semantic-role correction is required.
- Publish the Ratconfig child change, update only the locked Ratconfig revision in Yazelix, and update the Yazelix README LOC scorecard and CHANGELOG if project/runtime files change.

### Out of scope

- A user-configurable theme system, Mars palette changes, terminal-wide color remapping, product-specific branches in Ratconfig, or a duplicate palette in Yazelix.
- Claiming universal WCAG compliance from raw RGB values alone; terminal rendering and transparency still require dogfooding.
- Adding a color/contrast dependency for a small fixed palette.

## Implementation Notes

1. Capture the failing semantic roles before changing colors.
2. Extend or simplify `ConfigUiThemePalette` and `themed_style` so renderer call sites express roles rather than scattered light-mode exceptions.
3. Prefer deleting hard-coded role colors over adding per-widget overrides.
4. Add one focused renderer contract that exercises representative normal, selected, status, and detail roles in light appearance. Assert meaningful separation/readability, not a mirror of every literal RGB value.
5. Keep the generic Ratconfig boundary: no Yazelix tab names, paths, or product policy in the child.

## Verification

- In Ratconfig: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo test` pass.
- Focused renderer coverage fails on the current low-contrast role combinations and passes after the palette correction.
- Manual Mars dogfooding in light appearance confirms readable normal rows, selected rows, borders, metadata, errors/status, and details at the config popup's normal transparency.
- After publishing and locking Ratconfig in Yazelix: `nix flake check`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary-profile install pass.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop and capture a screenshot plus terminal color data if the problem is caused by Mars compositing rather than Ratconfig's emitted styles; move that failing layer to the correct owner.
- Stop if the fix requires a second theme/config surface or product-specific logic in Ratconfig.
- Stop if improved light contrast materially regresses dark appearance; separate the semantic roles before proceeding.

## Maintenance Notes

Owner: Ratconfig's renderer palette; Yazelix only consumes a published revision.

Effort: S/M. Risk: LOW. Confidence: HIGH.

Rejected alternatives: scattered per-widget light-mode overrides, changing Mars globally, duplicating the palette in Yazelix, and preserving exact RGB literals with mirror tests.
close_reason: Duplicate moved to ratconfig-light-mode-contrast-nh8. Ratconfig owns the renderer palette and semantic color roles; Yazelix remains the downstream dependency-pin and product-integration owner.

title: Dismiss visible popups when toggling the sidebar
description:
## Why

The sidebar toggle currently competes with a visible full-screen popup. After radar-first surfaces land, the useful intent is surface-neutral: dismiss the packaged popup and reveal the selected permanent rail if needed, without accidentally hiding an already-visible rail or inventing focus behavior for passive radar.

## User-visible contract

For Alt Shift H:

- With no visible packaged popup, preserve the selected surface's normal toggle behavior.
- With a visible packaged popup and a visible radar or Yazi rail, dismiss the popup and leave the rail visible.
- With a visible packaged popup and a hidden radar or Yazi rail, dismiss the popup and show the rail.
- With sidebar.surface = "none", dismiss a visible packaged popup and otherwise do nothing.
- Do not dismiss unrelated user floating panes, change Forest visibility, or move focus to a passive radar rail.

## Evidence

- defaults/zellij/config.kdl sends toggle_sidebar to the pane orchestrator.
- The pane orchestrator already owns semantic sidebar visibility resolution and its active-tab pane cache records title, floating, and suppressed state.
- The generic popup child owns popup lifecycle policies and distinguishes close-policy and hide-policy popups when displacing them.
- Radar surface child .3 removes direct Yazi sidebar-focus semantics, so this bead must not preserve the former focus restoration as a cross-surface contract.

## Scope

- Extend the pane-orchestrator sidebar command with one pure decision contract covering selected surface, popup visibility, and rail visibility.
- Dismiss only the visible packaged Yazelix popup identified from the active tab's pane manifest.
- Preserve the current no-popup toggle action for radar and Yazi and the harmless none behavior.
- Preserve keep-alive state for hide-policy popups and ensure required popup lifecycle hooks remain owned by the popup plugin.
- Publish any changed child first, update only its main-repository lock, and update the README LOC scorecard and CHANGELOG.

## Out of scope

- Hiding every floating pane, changing popup geometry, redesigning sidebar layouts, teaching the popup plugin sidebar geometry, changing Forest behavior, or adding a setting or keybinding.
- Coupling the generic popup child to Yazelix layout names, restoring direct sidebar focus, or duplicating popup close or hide hooks in two plugins.
- Folding in optional hide-on-file-open or columns-layout work.

## Implementation notes

1. Use a small resolver whose inputs are selected surface, visible packaged popup, and rail visibility; outputs are semantic popup dismissal and the existing rail visibility action.
2. Reuse the orchestrator active-tab pane cache and exact packaged-popup identity rule. Do not infer from focus alone.
3. Route dismissal through the popup-owned lifecycle action if direct suppression would bypass hooks.
4. Keep ordering deterministic: popup dismissal completes before the final rail action, without retries or sleeps.

## Verification

- One table-driven contract covers radar, Yazi, and none across no-popup, popup plus visible rail, and popup plus hidden rail cases.
- A non-popup floating pane remains visible and Forest is unaffected.
- Hide-policy popups retain process state; close-policy popups retain their lifecycle policy.
- Existing sidebar visibility, collapsed-base, missing-sidebar, and no-sidebar-mode checks continue to pass without asserting radar focus.
- Changed child formatting, tests, WASI and Nix builds pass; main flake, package, and temporary-profile checks pass.
- Manual dogfood covers config, agent, git, and menu popups with radar and Yazi initially visible and hidden when the user explicitly requests a GUI session.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if plugin-to-plugin dismissal cannot be ordered reliably in the current Zellij API; record the event trace before adding retries or sleeps.
- Stop if exact packaged popup identity cannot be distinguished from user floating panes using the existing manifest and configuration contract.
- Stop if implementation duplicates popup lifecycle policy or hooks in the pane orchestrator.
- Stop before adding Forest, optional file-open, or layout-family behavior.

## Maintenance notes

The pane orchestrator owns the contextual sidebar decision; the popup plugin remains the single owner of popup lifecycle semantics. Effort M, risk MED, confidence MED-HIGH.
acceptance_criteria:
- Alt Shift H preserves ordinary toggle behavior with no popup, dismisses only the visible packaged popup when present, and never hides a rail that was already visible.
- A hidden radar or Yazi rail is shown after popup dismissal; none dismisses the popup without creating a rail.
- Passive radar receives no focus action, direct Yazi focus semantics do not return, and Forest plus unrelated floating panes are unaffected.
- Popup close-versus-hide lifecycle remains behind the popup owner.
- One table-driven surface and visibility matrix plus focused child and main package checks pass.

title: Choose and deliver the v1 sidebar and navigation model
description:
## Goal

Choose Nova v1's sidebar and navigation model from direct evidence, then implement only the accepted result. The persistent Yazi popup and its Alt r reveal-or-hide contract are established; this program decides what, if anything, permanently occupies the sidebar rail and whether Forest earns a managed-Helix role.

## Sequence

1. Test upstream zj-radar with the packaged Yazelix runtime.
2. Test Forest against the exact packaged Helix and Steel surface, using the radar evidence as context.
3. Make one explicit product decision covering the permanent rail, navigation layers, defaults, and retained options.
4. Implement only that decision and dogfood it.
5. Reconcile the existing Yazelix tab-activity pipeline with the accepted ownership model.

## Ownership

Main Yazelix owns the product contract, root configuration, generated layout, key policy, documentation, and exact child pins. Zellij plugins own Zellij-native rail behavior. Managed Helix owns supported Steel integration. The persistent Yazi popup remains the editor-independent navigation and file-management surface.

## Constraints

Do not preselect radar, Forest, or a three-value sidebar setting in this epic. Do not fork either upstream before a concrete missing contract is demonstrated. Do not add arbitrary sidebar programs, a layout framework, ambient config mutation, runtime network installation, duplicate attention owners, or Forest dependencies to host-editor/no-Helix packages.

## Rejected alternatives

Deciding from repository descriptions instead of runtime evidence; implementing all candidate models behind configuration; keeping duplicate activity owners for compatibility; turning the proof into a general plugin system.
acceptance_criteria:
- The upstream zj-radar proof completes before the Forest proof.
- The Forest proof completes before the product decision.
- One decision records the accepted v1 rail, navigation layers, default, retained configuration choices, and ownership boundaries.
- Only accepted behavior is implemented; rejected candidate code and compatibility surfaces are not retained.
- Fresh-session dogfood covers the chosen model, the persistent Yazi popup, managed Helix, host-editor/no-Helix, narrow terminals, tab creation/switching, and relevant large repositories.
- The tab-activity pipeline is removed, retained, or narrowed explicitly so v1 has no duplicate attention owner.

title: Prove upstream zj-radar inside a disposable Yazelix session
description:
## Why

Before changing the packaged sidebar or creating a fork, Yazelix needs direct evidence that upstream zj-radar works with the Yazelix Zellij fork, generated layouts, isolated permission cache, and real agent producers. The repository currently has no zj-radar input or integration, while upstream v0.2.x is young and documents several load-bearing rules around per-tab instances, plugin permissions, pipe backpressure, and producer timeouts.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-zellij/Cargo.toml:74` pins Zellij 0.44.3, matching the upstream minimum.
- `runtime/yzx/runtime.rs:156-187,240` owns an isolated permission file and pre-seeds exact plugin locations.
- `defaults/zellij/layout.kdl:12-34` owns default and new-tab templates where one radar instance per tab must live.
- `runtime/yzx/zellij.rs:458-473` materializes runtime layouts and swap variants.
- https://github.com/marktoda/zj-radar/blob/main/docs/install.md documents Nix outputs, template requirements, permission-location behavior, and the 0.44.3 floor.
- https://github.com/marktoda/zj-radar/blob/main/docs/producers.md documents bounded Codex/Claude producers and the `zj_radar.status.v1` pipe.

## Scope

In scope:
- Pin a reviewed upstream zj-radar revision only if a committed build/check artifact is needed for the proof.
- Build the upstream WASM and CLI through Nix.
- Create a disposable, non-default Yazelix session/layout that uses radar with `naming "off"` and does not modify user Zellij, Codex, or Claude files.
- Prove default/new-tab behavior, swap-layout survival, isolated permission preauthorization, fake status payloads, real Codex producer behavior, tab switching, and clean session teardown.
- Record exact upstream revision, producer behavior, performance observations, and any required patch in this bead.

Out of scope:
- Do not change the packaged default sidebar, add `sidebar.surface`, remove Yazi, remove current activity markers, publish a fork, or add automatic ambient hook mutation.
- Do not keep a permanent development layout or public package output solely for the spike.

## Implementation Notes

1. Review the pinned upstream source and release notes; use its Nix outputs and public pipe contract directly.
2. Materialize all temporary config under a fresh temporary directory or temporary profile.
3. Seed required plugin permissions through the Yazelix-owned isolated cache rather than a stable home-directory symlink.
4. Test a synthetic payload before real Codex hooks so layout/plugin failures are separated from producer failures.
5. Prefer upstream configuration or a main-repository adapter-free composition. Propose a fork only if one concrete missing contract remains after the proof.

## Verification

- `nix build github:marktoda/zj-radar#default --no-link --print-build-logs` should build the WASM package.
- `nix build github:marktoda/zj-radar#zj-radar-cli --no-link --print-build-logs` should build the matching producer CLI.
- A disposable session should render radar in startup and newly created tabs, retain it through the packaged swap layouts, accept a bounded synthetic status pipe, and exit without touching ambient config.
- Real Codex activity should produce running, pending, and done transitions without blocked `zellij pipe` clients or leaked processes.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the proof would require editing ambient Zellij, Codex, or Claude configuration.
- Stop if any radar instance remains at a permission prompt or a producer send blocks beyond its documented timeout.
- Stop if radar mutates canonical Yazelix tab names with `naming "off"`.
- Stop before forking; record the smallest missing upstream contract and request the fork decision in this bead.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort: M. Risk: MED because this exercises a young external plugin and real hook backpressure. Confidence: HIGH that packaging and Zellij version fit; MED for producer onboarding.

Rejected alternatives: adopt latest unpinned; run `zj-radar setup zellij` against the user home; fork before the spike; infer agent state from polling.
acceptance_criteria:
- The exact upstream zj-radar revision and its Zellij compatibility, license, packages, permissions, layout requirements, pipe contract, and producer behavior are recorded.
- Upstream WASM and CLI build reproducibly through Nix without runtime network access or ambient configuration mutation.
- Deterministic non-GUI checks verify the disposable layout/config materialization, exact plugin location, isolated permission seed, and bounded producer command construction.
- A user-authorized disposable-session dogfood proves startup/new-tab placement, swap-layout survival, synthetic and real Codex status transitions, tab switching, bounded sends, and clean teardown.
- The result records concrete strengths, tradeoffs, failures, performance observations, and any smallest missing upstream contract.
- The proof changes no packaged default, creates no fork, and is sufficient input for the subsequent Forest comparison and final product decision.
notes: Repository runtime rule: do not launch the disposable GUI session unless the user explicitly requests dogfooding in that implementation turn. Otherwise complete the non-GUI build and static integration checks, record the exact manual session recipe, and leave runtime dogfood evidence pending.

title: Route editor reveal through the persistent Yazi popup
description:
## Why

Editor reveal must work independently of the tiled sidebar, but manual dogfood invalidated the first popup-address handshake. Opening an empty popup, registering its Yazi receiver through the pane orchestrator, polling readiness, and emitting reveal later produced intermittent failure, a visible Yazi error flash, and hidden-popup interference with Alt-h.

## User-visible contract

Alt r in the managed editor and yzx reveal <target> start the active tab persistent Yazi popup at the exact existing file or directory without changing the canonical workspace. Reveal deliberately replaces any existing popup process; ordinary Alt Shift Y toggles still preserve the live process and browsing state. A popup pane that exists while Zellij hides the floating layer must not divert Alt-h or Alt-l from tiled-pane navigation.

## Ownership

- yzpp is the sole popup lifecycle owner. A configured replace request may append runtime launch arguments while the configured spec remains the command and geometry owner.
- yzx-reveal validates and absolutizes one target, sends one replace request to yzpp, and reports the returned result.
- yzx-yazi and Yazi own startup target selection.
- The pane orchestrator owns only Alt-r editor routing and horizontal focus, using TabInfo.are_floating_panes_visible for popup visibility.

## Scope

- Pass the exact target as a runtime argument to the configured Yazi popup.
- Replace an absent, visible, or hidden popup through the same yzpp action.
- Delete popup YAZI_ID registration, readiness state, polling, sleeps, and receiver retry behavior.
- Keep sidebar registration, ordinary popup toggling, popup geometry, workspace semantics, and editor integration unchanged.
- Publish both child revisions before locking them into Nova.
- Update docs, CHANGELOG, contracts, and the LOC scorecard.

## Rejected alternatives

- Keep patching the cross-process readiness handshake.
- Reveal into a hidden live popup before showing it.
- Add a dedicated reveal plugin.
- Make the pane orchestrator own generic popup lifecycle.
- Fall back to the tiled sidebar or couple this feature to Forest.

## Verification

Run focused yzx-open and tutor tests; popup and orchestrator fmt, unit, WASI, and Nix checks; nix flake check; nix flake show --all-systems; the top-level Yazelix build; an isolated profile install; and the installed-runtime refresh. Fresh-session dogfood must cover absent, visible, and hidden popup reveal plus Alt-h with an open sidebar before stable promotion.
acceptance_criteria:
- One yzx reveal request sends one configured yzpp replace request containing the exact absolute target as a launch argument.
- Yazi starts at file and directory targets without popup YAZI_ID registration, readiness polling, sleeps, receiver retries, tiled-sidebar fallback, or workspace mutation.
- Reveal replaces an existing popup process; ordinary popup toggles preserve their existing keep-alive behavior.
- Hidden floating-layer state cannot make Alt-h or Alt-l treat a persistent popup as visible.
- Focused child and main checks pass, child revisions are published and locked, docs and LOC are current, and the installed runtime is refreshed.
- Fresh-session dogfood passes before the bead is closed or the change is promoted to stable.
notes:
Manual dogfood invalidated the first implementation: first reveal could flash a Yazi error, delivery was intermittent or absent, and a hidden persistent popup could divert Alt-h away from the visible sidebar. The readiness handshake has been removed. Published yzpp 48c5f4a adds request-local launch arguments to configured popup actions; published pane orchestrator f4733b0 deletes popup Yazi registration/readiness ownership and gates popup horizontal navigation on the active tab floating-layer visibility. Nova now sends one replace request with the absolute target and lets Yazi startup reveal it. This removes 113 tracked lines from the experimental implementation. Verification passed: popup 32 tests, fmt, WASI, Nix; orchestrator 77 tests, fmt, WASI, Nix; yzx-open 22 binary tests; tutor 13 tests; 103 Linux flake checks; all-system flake show; top-level package build; isolated profile install; and installed-profile refresh. Fresh-session dogfood on 2026-08-01 confirmed that reveal is very fast and reliable with the target-at-launch design.

Fresh-eyes simplification on 2026-08-01 removed the orphaned yzpp ensure action, unused main-repo sidebar_yazi_id and orchestrator_action helpers, redundant tab-map retention, and mechanical Clippy redundancies. Published yzpp 901b97c and pane orchestrator d781ef7; Nova locks both. The three-repo pass is net -52 tracked lines (main -4, child repos -48) with reveal semantics unchanged. Verification passed: popup 32 tests and Clippy; orchestrator 77 tests and all-target Clippy; yzx-open 22 binary tests; both child WASI and Nix builds; 100 Linux flake checks; all-system flake show; top-level package build; isolated profile install; and installed-profile refresh.

Second fresh-eyes pass on 2026-08-01 removed the remaining unused sidebar_yazi_state helper, collapsed identical left/right horizontal-focus ranking branches, and removed an internal cleanup note from the user-visible changelog. Published pane orchestrator ed983c0 and updated the Nova lock. This pass removes 17 tracked lines across the two repos with reveal and horizontal-focus behavior unchanged. Verification passed: yzx-open 22 binary tests and Clippy; orchestrator 77 tests, all-target Clippy, WASI, and Nix; 107 Linux flake checks; all-system flake show; top-level package build; isolated profile install; and installed-profile refresh.

Third fresh-eyes pass on 2026-08-01 replaced the one-consumer per-tab floating-layer visibility map with the active-tab boolean the horizontal-focus path actually needs. Published pane orchestrator 2c5d121 and updated only the experimental Nova lock. This removes 6 tracked Rust lines with identical TabUpdate timing, popup visibility, focus, response, and fallback behavior. The exported is_plugin and exited snapshot fields remain because the crate owns a standalone orchestration API; the tolerant optional sidebar-state parser also remains because typed deserialization would tighten malformed extension-field behavior for negligible simplification. Verification passed: orchestrator 77 tests, rustfmt, all-target Clippy, WASI, and Nix; the complete Linux flake suite; all-system flake show; top-level package build; isolated profile install; and installed-profile refresh.

Fourth fresh-eyes pass on 2026-08-01 removed the orphaned one-call focus_popup wrapper left after the popup ensure action was deleted. The unchanged focus, geometry, and response sequence now lives directly in show_popup; one localized Clippy argument-count allowance is explicit instead of preserving a ten-line forwarding helper to evade the heuristic. Published yzpp 3326e22 and updated only the experimental Nova lock. This removes 9 tracked Rust lines with popup actions, hooks, process lifecycle, geometry, response text, and ordering unchanged. A candidate removal of the yzx-open test mutex was rejected and reverted after a 100-run parallel stress check reproduced an ETXTBSY failure executing a generated Zellij shim on run 11; the lock remains a reliability boundary. Verification passed: popup 32 tests, rustfmt, all-target Clippy, WASI, and Nix; the complete Linux flake suite; all-system flake show; top-level package build; isolated profile install; and installed-profile refresh.
close_reason: Completed with published target-at-launch popup ownership; automated verification passed and fresh-session dogfood confirmed fast, reliable reveal

title: Implement and dogfood the accepted v1 navigation model
description:
## Goal

Implement exactly the sidebar/navigation contract chosen in the preceding decision and prove it through fresh-session dogfood. This bead is conditional on that decision; it does not assume radar, Forest, a Yazi sidebar option, or a particular default.

## Scope

- Change only the owners required by the accepted result: root configuration, generated Zellij layout/config, relevant child packages, managed Helix/Steel composition, key reference, Ratconfig inventory, docs, changelog, scorecard, and exact pins.
- Preserve the established persistent Yazi popup and Alt r reveal-or-hide contract unless the decision explicitly changes it.
- Add only configuration values the decision retained.
- Keep host-editor and no-Helix packages free of managed-Helix-only dependencies.
- Use upstream directly unless the decision identifies a concrete missing contract and assigns it to the correct child.

## Verification

Write the cheapest focused contract check before implementation, then run relevant child checks, Main flake check/show/build, a clean temporary-profile install, installed-profile refresh, and fresh-session interaction dogfood.

## Out of scope

No rejected candidate code, migration shim, arbitrary-sidebar abstraction, duplicate navigation owner, runtime plugin installer, or unrelated layout redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
- The implementation matches every accepted decision and contains no surface for rejected candidates.
- Configuration, layout, keys, docs, changelog, and scorecard agree on one contract.
- The persistent Yazi popup remains the universal navigation/file-management fallback unless explicitly revised by the decision.
- Managed Helix, host-editor, no-Helix, default/new tabs, narrow terminals, and relevant large repositories behave as decided.
- Focused checks and all relevant child/Main Nix gates pass.
- Fresh-session dogfood demonstrates the full accepted workflow and records any residual limitation before completion.

title: Reconcile tab-activity ownership with the accepted v1 model
description:
## Goal

After the accepted sidebar/navigation model is implemented, make the existing Yazelix tab-activity marker pipeline agree with the chosen attention owner. This is a reconciliation gate, not a precommitment to radar or deletion.

## Scope

- If the accepted model gives agent attention to radar or another owner, delete the duplicate activity-only tracking, transport, cache, formatting, configuration, tests, and documentation from the orchestrator and bar.
- If the accepted model retains the Yazelix marker as the sole owner, keep only the contract it still needs and record why.
- Preserve unrelated workspace/session state, tab names, native bells, bar behavior, agent popup behavior, and navigation.
- Reconcile yazelix-5vl-clear-hidden-tab-agent-activity-pgp: close as superseded if deletion makes it impossible, otherwise keep/fix it under the sole retained owner.
- Update child docs/checks and Main changelog/scorecard for any user-visible or LOC change.

## Rejected alternatives

Keeping two attention pipelines for compatibility; adapting the accepted owner through the old protocol merely to avoid deletion; deleting the pipeline before the product decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exactly one component owns agent/tab attention presentation under the accepted v1 model.
- Duplicate activity-only pipes, cache fields, formatter branches, settings, tests, and docs are deleted when they no longer serve the sole owner.
- If the existing marker survives, its unique role and retained contract are explicit and tested.
- Non-agent tab naming, selection, bells, bar rendering, workspace/session state, and popup behavior remain correct.

title: Choose the final v1 sidebar and navigation model
description:
## Decision

Using the completed upstream zj-radar and Forest proofs plus the already-dogfooded persistent Yazi popup, choose Nova v1's final sidebar and navigation model before implementation.

The decision must name:

- What permanently occupies the rail: radar, Yazi, nothing, or another result directly justified by the proofs.
- Whether Forest is adopted, deferred, or rejected for managed Helix.
- The default and every retained user-configurable option; do not retain candidates merely because they were tested.
- The role of the persistent Yazi popup across managed Helix, host-editor, and no-Helix packages.
- The visibility/focus keys and the owner of tab/agent attention.
- What happens to the current Yazelix tab-activity pipeline.
- Any exact upstream gap that justifies a child fork change.

## Decision standard

Prefer the fewest permanent surfaces and owners that preserve a coherent workflow. Consider narrow terminals, large repositories, startup/interaction latency, permissions, Steel composition, child maintenance, host-editor/no-Helix behavior, and actual dogfood. The implementation bead must be able to execute this decision without reopening product scope.

## Rejected alternatives

Implementing all candidates first; making Yazi survival or radar default a foregone conclusion; preserving duplicate options as a substitute for choosing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both proofs are complete and cited with their exact revisions and observed tradeoffs.
- The decision names the final rail, Forest disposition, popup role, default, complete configuration enum if any, keys, and attention owner.
- Every retained option has a concrete user need and test burden; rejected options require no compatibility surface.
- Managed Helix, host-editor, no-Helix, narrow-terminal, and large-repository behavior are explicit.
- Fork work is authorized only for a named missing upstream contract.
- The accepted contract is specific enough for one bounded implementation-and-dogfood bead.

title: Test Forest against packaged Helix and Steel
description:
## Goal

After the upstream zj-radar proof, determine whether Forest is a sound managed-Helix navigation layer in Nova. Test the exact packaged Helix and Steel surface rather than assuming upstream compatibility, and compare Forest with the proven radar behavior plus the established persistent Yazi popup.

## Scope

- Record exact Forest, notify.hx, glyph.hx, yazelix-helix, and Steel revisions, licenses, dependency edges, and required APIs.
- Build a disposable exact-pin prototype without Forge at runtime, floating inputs, startup network access, copied plugin sources, or user-home mutation.
- Prove one composition model in which packaged Steel helpers, optional Forest loading, and user Steel configuration do not silently replace each other.
- Exercise persistent/floating modes, current-file reveal, ordinary browsing, hidden/ignored files, Git status, mutations, refresh, refocus, narrow terminals, and ordinary/large repositories.
- Compare Forest open/closed with radar and the Yazi popup. Verify host-editor and no-Helix packages remain independent of Forest.
- Record an adopt, defer, or reject recommendation for the separate product-decision bead.

## Boundary

This proof does not permanently package or enable Forest, fork it, change Alt r, remove Yazi, create a general Steel plugin manager, or make the product decision. A small failing child-owned API contract may be recorded, but implementation waits for the final decision.

## Stop conditions

Stop on runtime network mutation, takeover of user Steel files, a broad Helix fork requirement, unsafe file mutation, or visibly blocking large-repository scanning.
acceptance_criteria:
- The radar proof is complete and its observations are used in the comparison.
- Exact Forest and transitive plugin revisions, licenses, APIs, and packaged Helix/Steel compatibility are recorded.
- A disposable exact-pin build and load smoke proves no runtime Forge/network dependency and no ambient user-config takeover.

- The UX/performance matrix covers both Forest modes, radar, Yazi popup, narrow terminals, ordinary and large repositories, file mutation safety, host-editor, and no-Helix workflows.

- The result records an evidence-backed adopt, defer, or reject recommendation; the separate decision bead makes the product choice.

title: Complete the Alt-r reveal and return round trip
description:
## Why

Target-at-launch made Helix-to-Yazi reveal fast and reliable. After dogfooding the reverse direction, the simpler mental model won: Alt r reveals when pressed in Helix and returns when pressed in Yazi. Returning must preserve the current editor state and, for the popup role, preserve live Yazi navigation state.

## User-visible contract

- Alt r in managed Helix reveals the current buffer in the active-tab persistent Yazi popup.
- Alt r in the popup Yazi hides the popup, preserves its process and navigation state, and returns to the pane underneath unchanged.
- Alt r in tiled Yazi focuses the existing managed editor and leaves tiled Yazi visible.
- Alt r in Yazi never opens the hovered item or changes editor cwd, tab workspace, sidebar cwd, or editor buffers.
- Enter remains the explicit Yazi action for opening an item.
- One chord performs exactly one role-local action and cannot replay after focus changes.

## Ownership

- Helix owns its local editor-to-Yazi reveal binding.
- Managed Yazi owns its local return binding and passes no hovered path.
- The Yazi return helper owns the role decision: popup sends one explicit hide to yzpp; tiled Yazi sends one focus_editor action to the pane orchestrator.
- yzpp solely owns persistent popup lifecycle and state preservation.
- The pane orchestrator solely owns tiled editor focus.
- yzx-open owns ordinary and retargeted open delivery only; it owns no reverse-return intent.
- Zellij deliberately has no Alt r binding.

## Scope

Remove the hovered-path argument, private reveal-editor intent, reverse bridge delivery, optional working-directory payloads, reverse-specific tests, and reverse-open documentation. Retain the generic explicit popup hide action, the persistent popup process, and the local Yazi key binding.

## Rejected alternatives

Do not open the hovered item on return, reuse Enter semantics, pass the hovered path, close and recreate the popup by default, mutate cwd or workspace state, create an editor pane, restore global Zellij routing, or add another router or plugin owner.

## Verification

Run focused yzx-open format, unit, and clippy checks; keymap and materialization contracts; complete flake check and all-system show; top-level build; isolated profile install; installed runtime refresh; exact LOC scorecard; and diff checks. Fresh-session dogfood is required before closing this bead or promoting to stable.
notes:
The user superseded the earlier no-side-effect reverse-reveal design after re-evaluating the workflow. The prior implementation proved technically reliable, but opening the hovered file gave Alt r a surprising second meaning and forced users to remember another dismissal chord. The chosen contract is reveal from Helix and return unchanged from Yazi. The obsolete private --reveal-editor intent, hovered-path argument, reverse bridge path, optional working-directory payload, reverse-specific tests, and corresponding documentation were deleted rather than retained as dormant compatibility.

The final implementation removes 225 tracked project lines: 223 Rust lines and 2 Markdown lines. Focused TDD first reproduced the popup hide plus editor-focus bug, then passed with exact role-local calls. Verification passes: rustfmt, all 23 yzx-open tests, clippy with warnings denied, tutor checks, the complete 106-check flake suite, all-system flake show, top-level Yazelix build, isolated profile install, installed runtime refresh, packaged keymap inspection, exact 25,824-line scorecard, stale-symbol search, and git diff checks. On 2026-08-02, the user reported that the feature had worked extremely well throughout fresh-session dogfood. The runtime acceptance gate is satisfied.
close_reason: Completed and accepted after successful fresh-session dogfood

title: Make Ratconfig field columns width-aware
description:
## Why

Ratconfig's default three-column field list reserves 18 cells for `takes effect`, 44 for `setting`, and only 28 for `value`. In the normal half-screen config popup this leaves a large empty gap after short setting labels while structured values and long paths are truncated much earlier than necessary. The list should remain a compact comparison surface, but it should use the width it actually has.

## Evidence

- Runtime dogfooding report on 2026-07-14: the Yazi tab shows a conspicuous gap before `value`, while flavor, opener, plugin, and native-file values truncate despite unused horizontal space.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:11-13` hard-codes the default field widths to 18, 44, and 28.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:316-338` gives the list half the terminal width and passes that rectangle into `render_list`.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:338-375` knows the list's exact inner width, but headers and rows are built without using it.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:613-634` pads every setting to 44 cells and truncates every value at 28.
- `crates/yzx-config/src/model.rs:147-159` supplies a custom table only for Keys, so the Yazi tab correctly exercises Ratconfig's default field layout.

## User-Visible Contract

The default `takes effect | setting | value` list stays column-aligned across a tab, avoids visible padding far beyond the tab's actual labels, and gives `value` all useful remaining width. Values may still end in an ellipsis because the list is a preview, but unused setting padding must not force premature truncation. Layout remains readable without overflow at representative wide, medium, and narrow popup widths.

## Scope

In scope:
- Change Ratconfig's default field-list geometry in `src/render.rs` to resolve widths from the available list width and tab content.
- Keep column positions stable while moving selection and while entering or clearing search; avoid distracting width jitter.
- Give the value column the remaining usable width after bounded status and setting columns.
- Preserve explicit host-supplied `ConfigUiListTable` behavior and Advanced status-table behavior.
- Add focused renderer contracts for width allocation, alignment, truncation, and narrow boundaries.
- Publish the Ratconfig child change, update only the locked Ratconfig revision in Yazelix, and update Yazelix's CHANGELOG and LOC scorecard as required.

Out of scope:
- Do not remove or abbreviate the `takes effect` column.
- Do not add horizontal scrolling, resizable panes, a detail-only mode, or a six-column TOML table to Yazi.
- Do not change the 50/50 body split in this slice.
- Do not change colors or include the separate light-mode contrast bead.
- Do not add Yazelix/Yazi-specific layout rules to Ratconfig.

## Implementation Notes

1. Add one small pure width resolver whose inputs are available inner width and the default field rows for the selected tab.
2. Use explicit minimums and caps for status and setting; allocate the remainder to value. Derive stable tab widths rather than selection-dependent widths.
3. Pass the resolved widths through both header and row rendering so alignment has one owner.
4. Preserve section headings, file-action rows, invalid-state styling, and custom host table rendering.
5. Rust dependency decision: use Ratatui and standard-library width information already present. Add no crate.

## Verification

- In Ratconfig, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` should exit 0.
- In Ratconfig, `cargo test` should exit 0.
- Focused renderer tests should prove a screenshot-equivalent width gives the value column materially more than 28 cells when setting labels are short, headers and rows share exact boundaries, narrow layouts do not overflow, and search/selection do not shift column starts.
- Existing custom table and Advanced status-table tests should remain unchanged or pass with equivalent behavior.
- After publishing and locking Ratconfig in Yazelix, `nix flake check` and `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` should succeed.
- `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` should install the updated package.
- Manual dogfooding should inspect ordinary scalar tabs, the Yazi tab's structured previews and file paths, and a narrow popup.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the proposal changes explicit host-supplied table widths; keep that as a separate contract.
- Stop if width allocation requires storing terminal geometry in the model; keep geometry in Ratconfig's renderer.
- Stop if a narrow layout can only be made safe by silently deleting a semantic column; bring that responsive-boundary decision back to the maintainer.
- Stop if the implementation begins changing detail rendering or contrast; those have separate beads.

## Maintenance Notes

Owner: Ratconfig's generic default field-list renderer. Yazelix remains a consumer and lock owner.

Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM because this changes geometry across every default Ratconfig tab. Confidence: HIGH.

Rejected alternatives: one new fixed width tuple, horizontal scrolling, removing `takes effect`, changing the pane split, enabling the six-column TOML table, and adding Yazi-specific rendering.
close_reason: Duplicate moved to ratconfig-width-aware-field-columns-g6g. Ratconfig owns default field-list geometry; Yazelix remains the downstream dependency-pin and product-integration owner.

title: Pretty-print structured Ratconfig detail values
description:
## Why

Ratconfig renders structured TOML values as compact JSON-like strings in the details pane. Long objects and arrays wrap as dense walls of text, and when an effective value equals its default the same large payload is printed twice. The left list may remain a truncated preview, but the details pane should be the complete, readable inspection surface.

## Evidence

- Runtime dogfooding report on 2026-07-14: Yazi's `opener` object wraps across several opaque lines in details, and identical `current` and `default` objects are duplicated.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:466-488` wraps the final detail lines as ordinary paragraph text without structured-value layout.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:692-700` renders `current` and `default` unconditionally through the same one-line helper.
- `../ratconfig/src/render.rs:1228-1232` concatenates a fixed-width label and an opaque string value into one line.
- `../ratconfig/src/model.rs:794-810` stores compact rendered current/default TOML values, including structured tables and arrays.
- `../ratconfig/src/model.rs:817-834` reuses those compact strings both for list cells and field details, so the renderer currently has no distinct expanded representation.

## User-Visible Contract

Scalar current/default values remain compact. Structured objects and arrays render in the details pane as complete, indented, multiline values with no truncation. Long nested strings wrap without destroying the visible structure. If current and default are identical, the default line says `same as current` instead of repeating the payload. Non-JSON TOML values such as infinities and NaN remain complete and inspectable through a safe fallback.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add a generic structured-value detail representation in Ratconfig for objects and arrays.
- Pretty-print current and default structures with stable indentation and readable wrapping.
- Deduplicate identical effective/default payloads while preserving the distinction between explicit, defaulted, and unset state.
- Keep scalars and ordinary metadata in the current compact key/value form.
- Preserve complete TOML special values that cannot be represented by strict JSON.
- Add focused renderer/model tests for nested objects, arrays, long strings, identical defaults, differing defaults, and TOML infinity/NaN fallback.
- Publish the Ratconfig child change, update only the locked Ratconfig revision in Yazelix, and update Yazelix's CHANGELOG and LOC scorecard as required.

Out of scope:
- Do not change list-column widths or list preview truncation; that is the adaptive-columns bead.
- Do not add JSON/TOML editing, syntax highlighting, a copy mode, scrolling, or a detail-only pane mode.
- Do not render the entire source file or replace the existing `e` source-file action.
- Do not introduce Yazi-specific labels, semantic summaries, or paths into Ratconfig.
- Do not include the separate contrast work.

## Implementation Notes

1. Keep compact list previews and expanded detail rendering as two presentations of one field value.
2. Prefer carrying or deriving structured data at the generic Ratconfig model/builder boundary rather than blindly treating every rendered string as JSON.
3. If safe structured data is unavailable for a host-built field, preserve the existing complete wrapped string instead of guessing.
4. Render structured labels on their own line followed by indented content; keep scalar labels and values on one line.
5. When `current_value == default_value` and a real default exists, render the current value once and use `default  same as current`.
6. Rust dependency decision: reuse Ratconfig's existing `serde_json`/`toml` stack and Ratatui text primitives. Add no crate.

## Verification

- In Ratconfig, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` should exit 0.
- In Ratconfig, `cargo test` should exit 0.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the only approach reparses every display string as strict JSON and loses valid TOML values; add a bounded generic representation or preserve the raw fallback.

Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM because the model must preserve complete TOML values while improving generic rendering. Confidence: HIGH in the UX defect and MEDIUM/HIGH in the smallest representation.

Rejected alternatives: leaving opaque wrapped JSON, count-only summaries, flattening every object into dotted paths, rendering the whole source file, adding a detail-focus mode in the first slice, and strict-JSON-only reparsing.

title: Remove duplicate agent-usage scheduling from the pane orchestrator
description:
## Why

`yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator` contains a second agent-usage refresh scheduler even though `yazelix-zellij-bar` already owns provider invocation, cache freshness, singleflight, backoff, and rendering. Current Nova does not provide the `YAZELIX_YZX_CONTROL_BIN` or `YAZELIX_RUNTIME_DIR/libexec/yzx_control` contract required by that scheduler, so the path is unwired while still carrying timers, provider configuration, process launches, and heartbeat fields. After the bar safety contract is fixed, keeping the second owner adds LOC and creates a future risk that an environment change accidentally activates competing refresh policy.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/status_bar_cache.rs:18-31` defines independent 10-second refresh intervals, max ages, timeouts, and backoffs for three usage providers.
- `../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/status_bar_cache.rs:140-320` schedules timers and launches `yzx_control zellij status-cache-refresh-*-usage`.
- `../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src/status_bar_cache_contract.rs:31-46` can resolve that command only from `YAZELIX_YZX_CONTROL_BIN` or `YAZELIX_RUNTIME_DIR`.
- Current Nova source has no producer for either environment contract. The packaged `yzx` runtime is the small local Rust command in `runtime/yzx`, not the former `yzx_control` runtime.
- `../yazelix-zellij-bar/src/lib.rs:963-994,1263-1373` already owns refresh and cache policy.
- `../yazelix-zellij-bar/presets/yazelix_runtime_bar.template.kdl:32-48` invokes the cache-owning widget commands directly.

## Architecture Contract

The pane orchestrator owns pane, workspace, tab-activity, and status-bus facts. It does not schedule external agent-usage providers. The bar widget remains the single owner of agent-usage invocation, cache, stale behavior, timeout, and rendering. Removing the duplicate path must not change the visible bar, provider selection, workspace status, tab activity, pane behavior, or heartbeat facts unrelated to agent refresh.

## Scope

In scope:
- Confirm no supported current consumer supplies the two legacy runtime variables for agent-usage refresh.
- Remove Claude, Codex, and OpenCode usage refresh timers, next-refresh state, provider-refresh launches, and scheduler-only configuration from `yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator`.
- Remove heartbeat fields/tests that exist only to report those removed refresh attempts.
- Keep all workspace/status cache writes and tab-activity/status-pipe behavior.
- Publish and pin the accepted child revision in Yazelix; update the README LOC scorecard and `CHANGELOG.md` only where the changed public/runtime contract requires it.

Out of scope:
- Do not change bar widget cache policy, provider commands, rendering, repaint intervals, Zellij layout, pane policy, or legacy compatibility.
- Do not broaden this bead into deleting the generic `status-cache-write`, workspace or tab-activity pipe, or remaining `yzx_control` runtime contract; those carry non-usage behavior and require separate evidence and user scope.
- Do not replace the scheduler with another background task, daemon, watcher, shell wrapper, or main-owned implementation.
- Do not remove general pane-orchestrator heartbeat or status cache diagnostics that remain useful for pane/workspace behavior.

## Implementation Notes

1. Land after `yazelix-8u5-4-hnv.1` so the surviving bar owner has the bounded retry contract.
2. Trace each usage-scheduler field to prove it has no non-agent consumer, then delete the full path instead of leaving compatibility stubs.
3. Prefer net-negative LOC. Add no crates, flags, environment variables, or replacement abstractions.
4. If a supported consumer is found, stop and record its exact runtime contract rather than preserving speculative compatibility.

## Verification

- `cd ../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator && cargo fmt --all -- --check` should exit 0.
- `cd ../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator && cargo test --lib` should exit 0 with workspace, status cache, tab activity, pane, and remaining heartbeat contracts intact.
- `cd ../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator && cargo build --target wasm32-wasip1 --profile release` and `nix build .#yazelix_zellij_pane_orchestrator --no-link` should exit 0.
- `rg -n "status-cache-refresh-(claude|codex|opencode-go)-usage|USAGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL|status_usage_provider" ../yazelix-zellij-pane-orchestrator/src` should find no live scheduler surface.
- `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs`, and a temporary profile install should succeed after the child pin.
- Fresh-session dogfood should show unchanged bar output, workspace labels, tab activity, and pane behavior.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if current Nova or another explicitly supported consumer relies on this scheduler; report the producer and user-visible need before changing scope.
- Stop if removal would move provider logic into main Yazelix or the pane orchestrator.
- Stop if the bar safety bead is incomplete.
- Stop if workspace, activity, or pane behavior would need redesign.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S/M, risk MED, confidence MED/HIGH. Expected LOC is negative. This is a post-safety simplification and does not block Beta 4. Rejected: reconnecting the legacy `yzx_control` path, adding new Nova runtime variables solely to activate it, or retaining inert compatibility shims.
acceptance_criteria:
- A repository-wide consumer check finds no supported current producer of the three agent-usage scheduler commands; finding one triggers the documented stop condition instead of speculative compatibility.
- Claude, Codex, and OpenCode usage-only configuration, deadlines, timers, process launches, and dead tests are removed with net-negative LOC and no replacement abstraction or dependency.
- Generic status-cache-write behavior, workspace and tab-activity pipes, non-usage heartbeat facts, pane behavior, and timer scheduling for surviving features remain unchanged.
- cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo test --lib, the wasm32-wasip1 release build, and nix build .#yazelix_zellij_pane_orchestrator --no-link pass in the child.
- The published child revision is pinned in Yazelix; main flake, package, and profile checks pass; fresh-session dogfood shows unchanged bar, workspace, activity, and pane behavior.
notes: Implemented the ownership cleanup in pane-orchestrator commits db5a34296ec388226cdc9448513e2009222f56ee and 17e870d5eefbeec0b84a62fbe11b533fd50227bb. The first deletes Claude, Codex, and OpenCode usage-only configuration, deadlines, timers, launches, provider contract, and heartbeat refresh facts. The second bounded fresh-eyes pass removes the rejected global Alt-z popup receiver path that still existed on child main but was deliberately not consumed by Yazelix; workspace popup toggle behavior now matches the accepted pre-Alt-z baseline exactly. Relative to pinned baseline 8d4712a6a8380d8b2ddcd241ae91aedfbf6896b3, the child changes 7 files with 5 insertions and 353 deletions. Repository-wide searches find no supported Nova producer or consumer for the removed scheduler or picker paths. Generic status-cache writes, workspace/status pipes, tab activity, pane behavior, and non-usage heartbeat facts remain. Child fmt, 77 library tests, WASI release build, and Nix package build pass. An extra Clippy -D warnings run reports three pre-existing warnings in untouched active_tab_session_state.rs, sidebar_contract.rs, and an ai_pane_activity_contract.rs test; left unchanged to keep the fork pass bounded. Yazelix pins 17e870d5eefbeec0b84a62fbe11b533fd50227bb; exact LOC recount is 24,738; flake check, flake show --all-systems, package build, temporary-profile install, and diff validation pass. Fresh-session interaction dogfood remains pending because AGENTS.md prohibits launching a session unless the user requests it.
close_reason: Completed: removed duplicate pane-owned agent-usage scheduling with 353 net child lines deleted, published and pinned the simplified pane-orchestrator revision, passed all child and Yazelix automated gates, refreshed the installed runtime, and the maintainer confirmed fresh-session behavior is working well.

title: Allow user replacement of packaged Starship Yazi plugin
description:
## Why

GitHub issue #668 reports that Nova rejects a user-managed `starship.yazi` because the same plugin name is packaged. User-only plugin names already work, but this collision blocks a valid migration and forces users to abandon their `ya pkg`-managed Starship plugin.

Yazi defines each `name.yazi/` directory as one plugin package with `main.lua` as its entry point. Recursively merging two plugin directories would create an unversioned hybrid package, so replacement must be whole-directory and deliberately limited to the replaceable Starship visual integration; navigation and sidebar integrations remain protected.

## User-visible contract

A managed user `starship.yazi` directory replaces Nova’s packaged `starship.yazi` as one complete plugin package in the generated runtime. User plugins with new names continue to work. Collisions with Yazelix integration-owned plugins fail clearly and atomically. Sources are never modified.

## Evidence

- `crates/yzx-yazi-config/src/main.rs:232`: asset materialization currently overlays user plugin and flavor directories.
- `crates/yzx-yazi-config/src/main.rs:276`: every packaged plugin collision currently fails.
- `flake.nix:381`: Nova packages integration-owned sidebar plugins plus auto-layout, Git, and Starship plugins.
- `defaults/yazi/init.lua:1`: packaged plugins are loaded as runtime behavior.
- https://github.com/luccahuguet/yazelix/issues/668 contains the migration report.
- Yazi plugin documentation treats each `.yazi` directory as one package; `ya pkg` installs and locks complete plugin directories.

## Scope

In scope:
- Permit whole-directory user replacement of packaged `starship.yazi`.
- Preserve atomic staging and source/runtime overlap checks.
- Keep user-only plugins and same-name flavor replacement unchanged.
- Improve the protected collision diagnostic.
- Add focused tests proving complete replacement rather than recursive merging, and protected-plugin refusal without runtime damage.
- Update configuration docs, CHANGELOG, and LOC scorecard.

Out of scope:
- Recursive plugin directory merging.
- Replacement of sidebar-state, sidebar-status, zoxide-editor, Git, or auto-layout plugins.
- A user-facing allowlist setting, general plugin policy framework, package installer, migration command, or compatibility layer.
- Changes to Yazi, `ya pkg`, Home Manager plugin options, flavors, or the plugin initialization order.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/yzx-yazi-config/Cargo.toml -- --check` exits 0.
- `cargo test --manifest-path crates/yzx-yazi-config/Cargo.toml` exits 0 and proves replacement/refusal contracts.
- `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.yzx_yazi_materialization --no-link` exits 0.
- `nix flake check` exits 0.
- `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` exits 0.
- `nix profile add --refresh /home/lucca/pjs/yazelix-dir/yazelix --profile <tmp>` succeeds.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if replacement requires recursive plugin merging.
- Stop if a replacement cannot preserve Nova’s Starship setup and refresh calls without a compatibility shim.
- Stop if protected collisions can partially replace the existing generated runtime.
- Stop before adding a general plugin policy or Home Manager surface.

## Maintenance Notes

Yazelix owns the small replaceability decision; Yazi owns plugin package semantics. Rejected: recursive merge, unrestricted replacement, and preserving Classic compatibility as an independent contract. Effort S, risk LOW/MED, confidence HIGH.
notes: Final fresh-eyes and simplification pass: corrected contradictory changelog wording to say other packaged plugins, since Starship is also integrated; removed a duplicate atomicity assertion while retaining the distinct validation and general staging proof; and collapsed fixture directory creation plus copy into one install operation. Final reviewed shape is 22 tracked lines smaller than the first hardened version, moving from 19,301 to 19,279 lines, with unchanged runtime behavior. Rejected broader plugin validation, invalid packaged fixtures, nested-content symlink policy, Lua setup rewriting, and generic replacement configuration as behavior changes or complexity increases. Rust, Clippy, exact Yazi materialization and startup, full flake checks, and all-system evaluation pass.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes and simplification passes complete; replacement remains narrow, atomic, tested through real Yazi startup, and 17 tracked lines smaller.
