title: Build a mathematical animation collection for Yazelix Screen
description:
## Why

`yzs` already proves that native terminal animation can make the Yazelix welcome surface distinctive, but its built-in collection is concentrated in boids, Game of Life, and Mandelbrot variants. A coherent mathematical-art collection would add visibly different motion families while preserving the standalone plain-terminal contract.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-screen/src/screen_runner.rs` lists the current styles and owns CLI dispatch.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/lib.rs` exposes a foreground-only `ScreenCell`; `terminal_control.rs` has background styling only as a private output helper.
- `../yazelix-screen/Cargo.toml` currently needs only `crossterm`.
- Main Yazelix consumes the published `yzs` package through `flake.nix` and the `yazelixScreen` revision in `flake.lock`.
- FrankenTUI documents compact equations for Plasma, Gray-Scott, Clifford attractors, and radial wave interference at https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui.

## Scope

In scope:
- Deliver two enabling slices: reusable truecolor half-block field rendering and narrow scalar-density simulation helpers.
- Deliver native styles for multi-scale Turing patterns, primordial particle systems, Chladni cymatics, complex domain coloring, an attractor atlas, quasicrystal interference, Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion, Matrix rain, plasma, radial wave interference, Physarum trail networks, and later Lenia.
- Keep each effect independently selectable from `yzs`, bounded by the shared animation lifecycle, and usable outside Yazelix.
- Treat child publication and the main flake-pin update as an explicit integration boundary.

Out of scope:
- Do not migrate `yzs` to Ratatui, FrankenTUI, Kitty graphics, Sixel, or an image-backed renderer.
- Do not change main Yazelix welcome/session policy or make every new style part of the random pool without an explicit visual and performance decision.
- Do not combine all effects into one unreviewable implementation.
- Do not begin Lenia until the density-helper and Physarum slices provide real performance evidence.

## Implementation Notes

The half-block renderer blocks all dense field effects. Scalar-density helpers follow it and block Physarum and Lenia. Native Matrix rain is independent. Plasma and radial wave interference remain separate from quasicrystal plane waves. Land one effect at a time, reuse existing timing/input/resize ownership, and require a concrete dependency justification before adding crates.

## Verification

- Every completed child passes the standalone command floor in `../yazelix-screen/AGENTS.md`.
- Each exposed style renders nonblank deterministic test frames at small, normal, and resized dimensions without panics or stale cells.
- Each simulation has a representative frame-time or bounded-work check appropriate to its complexity.
- Published child revisions are pinned by main Yazelix before integrated runtime claims are closed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop an effect if it requires host-terminal ownership, unbounded state, or a non-terminal graphics protocol.
- Split work further if a child cannot be reviewed and visually validated independently.
- Keep Lenia deferred if direct convolution cannot meet cadence after the shared helpers are proven.

## Maintenance Notes

Accepted after comparing formula-driven, fractal, artificial-life, and terminal-native candidates. Deferred alternatives include a general VFX framework migration, image-backed backgrounds, host-terminal shaders, and external aquarium/rain processes.
close_reason: Migrated without contract changes to child-owned epic yzs-mathematical-animation-collection-dou in yazelix-screen; the child repository is the sole active planning owner.

title: Generalize Yazelix Screen to render truecolor half-block fields
description:
## Why

Most proposed field effects need two independently colored vertical samples per terminal cell. The current `ScreenCell` stores one glyph and one foreground RGB color, forcing effect-specific packing and preventing a reusable truecolor field surface.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-screen/src/lib.rs` defines `ScreenCell { glyph, color_x, color_y }` and the sparse `ScreenFrame` render closure.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/terminal_control.rs` already emits a foreground/background-styled glyph through a private helper.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` contains local half-block and background-tone logic that demonstrates both the visual value and the duplication risk.

## Scope

In scope:
- Extend the frame/cell contract so a cell can carry explicit foreground and background colors without effect-owned ANSI strings.
- Add a reusable dense field adapter that maps upper and lower RGB samples to `▀`, clips odd pixel heights, clears stale output, and reuses allocations across frames.
- Preserve ordinary single-color glyph rendering for existing styles.
- Define behavior for transparent/absent samples, zero-sized terminals, resizes, and color reset at row/frame boundaries.
- Add focused renderer tests and one small example or test fixture that makes visual inspection easy.

Out of scope:
- No Ratatui/FrankenTUI migration, image protocol, alpha compositing, sixel canvas, or general scene graph.
- Do not redesign every existing animation around the new adapter.
- Do not add a rendering crate unless measurement proves the current crossterm path insufficient.

## Implementation Notes

Keep terminal emission centralized in `terminal_control.rs`. Prefer a typed optional background on `ScreenCell` plus a field-to-frame adapter over preformatted escape sequences. Ensure Unicode width remains exactly one column.

## Verification

- Unit tests cover upper/lower color placement, missing halves, odd dimensions, clipping, resize shrinkage, and reset sequences.
- Existing styles remain byte/behavior compatible where practical and render without color leakage.
- Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test`, `cargo check --examples`, `cargo run --example render_once`, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link` in the child.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the API requires effects to construct raw ANSI.
- Stop and benchmark before adopting a broader rendering dependency.

## Maintenance Notes

This is a P1 enabling slice, not a user-facing style. Publish it before dependent effects; update the main pin only when a published consumer revision needs it.

title: Add reusable scalar-density simulation helpers
description:
## Why

The half-block renderer converts finished samples into terminal cells, but particle trails and continuous cellular automata also need efficient scalar-field operations before color mapping. Implementing deposition, wrapped sampling, decay, and blur independently in Physarum and Lenia would duplicate the most error-prone numerical plumbing.

## Evidence

- The renderer foundation owns RGB sample emission, not simulation-field evolution.
- The Physarum particle model needs trail deposition, sensor sampling, diffusion, and decay.
- Lenia needs reusable wrapped scalar fields and bounded convolution over continuous cell values.
- Existing `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` and `game_of_life.rs` each own specialized spatial state, with no general density-field helper.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add a small reusable contiguous scalar field with explicit width/height and allocation reuse.
- Support clear/fill, wrapped and clipped sampling, bounded additive deposition, decay, normalization, and one measured local blur/convolution path.
- Define resize behavior and prevent NaN/infinite values from entering palettes or terminal output.
- Provide adapters that let an effect map the scalar field through the half-block renderer without coupling simulation math to ANSI emission.

Out of scope:
- No generic tensor library, FFT framework, GPU path, arbitrary kernels API, scene graph, or replacement for effect-owned update equations.
- Do not force Gray-Scott or Turing patterns onto helpers that make their double-buffered update less clear.

## Implementation Notes

Keep the abstraction narrow and data-oriented. Prefer reusable scratch buffers and explicit boundary modes. Benchmark local blur before selecting a separable or summed-area implementation; do not add a numerical crate by default.

## Verification

- Tests cover indexing, wrapped/clipped edges, conservation for deposition before decay, blur symmetry, normalization, resize reset, finite-value defense, and buffer reuse.
- Benchmarks or timing tests establish a practical budget at representative 120x40 and 200x60 logical fields.
- Run the full standalone child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the abstraction starts encoding Physarum or Lenia rules directly.
- Stop and keep an effect-local implementation if a supposedly generic operation has only one real consumer or worsens clarity/performance.

## Maintenance Notes

This is the explicit later-stage prerequisite requested for density-heavy effects. It depends on the half-block renderer; Physarum and Lenia depend on this task.

title: Add a plasma interference animation
description:
## Why

A classic plasma effect produces smooth psychedelic bands from a few moving sine fields. It is cheap, immediately animated, and visually distinct from cellular automata, particles, fractals, and radial wave interference.

## Evidence

- FrankenTUI documents its Plasma effect as the average of six animated sine phases in its VFX catalog: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui.
- The shared truecolor half-block renderer can preserve smooth gradients without full-cell vertical stretching.

## Scope

In scope:
- Combine a small curated set of spatial and radial sine terms over aspect-correct normalized coordinates.
- Animate phase and color cycling smoothly with bounded speed and no frame-wide flashes.
- Map the normalized field through a truecolor palette and add one `plasma` CLI style.
- Precompute frame-invariant coordinate terms and avoid per-cell allocation.

Out of scope:
- No shader runtime, arbitrary formula editor, audio reactivity, or direct FrankenTUI dependency.
- Do not merge this with radial `wave-interference`; they must retain different spatial structure.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and an explicit random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, resize, and terminal cleanup. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Use FrankenTUI as a behavioral reference and implement the compact equation locally after checking provenance. Standard-library trigonometry should be sufficient.

## Verification

- Tests cover deterministic phase evolution, finite normalized samples, aspect correction, palette bounds, and resize regeneration.
- Visual fixtures confirm smooth bands, continuous color motion, and a nonblank frame at small, normal, and wide sizes.
- Run the full child command floor and inspect the real truecolor runtime.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if palette cycling causes flicker or abrupt global luminance changes.
- Stop if the result is visually interchangeable with quasicrystal or radial wave interference.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked only by the half-block renderer. Add no VFX or math crate.
close_reason: Migrated without contract changes to child-owned epic yzs-mathematical-animation-collection-dou in yazelix-screen; the child repository is the sole active planning owner.

title: Add a radial wave-interference animation
description:
## Why

Multiple moving wave sources create expanding, colliding ripple fronts and moire-like nodes. This is a separate visual family from quasicrystal plane waves and plasma color bands, and it can react naturally to terminal geometry.

## Evidence

- FrankenTUI documents Wave Interference as `I(x,t) = sum sin(k_i * |x-s_i| - omega_i*t)` in its VFX catalog: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui.
- The existing quasicrystal bead uses oriented plane waves; radial distance to discrete sources yields materially different concentric collisions.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement a bounded set of radial wave sources with curated frequency, phase, amplitude, and slow source motion.
- Correct distance for terminal aspect ratio and map signed interference to a stable truecolor palette.
- Keep source count and per-frame work bounded; precompute or reuse coordinate data where useful.
- Add one `wave-interference` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No physical fluid solver, reflection/refraction model, interactive mouse sources, audio input, or arbitrary source editor.
- Do not collapse the bead into plasma or quasicrystal rendering.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and an explicit random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, resize, and terminal cleanup. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx screen` path.
Implement the equation locally from the documented model. Keep wave-source state typed and deterministic.

## Verification

- Tests cover source-distance symmetry, deterministic motion, finite amplitudes, aspect correction, resize handling, and palette bounds.
- Visual fixtures show recognizable circular fronts and changing interference nodes at narrow, normal, and wide sizes.
- Run the full child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if source motion produces discontinuities or global flashing.
- Stop if terminal aspect correction leaves circles visibly elliptical in the supported runtime.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: blocked by the half-block renderer. Standard-library math is sufficient.

title: Add a Physarum trail-network animation
description:

- Render trail intensity and fresh deposits through a restrained truecolor palette.
- Add one `physarum` CLI style.

Out of scope:

title: Add a deferred Lenia continuous-life animation

- Use wrapped boundaries, reusable scalar fields, and the half-block renderer.
- Preserve recognizable localized structures through resize by deterministic restart rather than malformed resampling.
- Add one `lenia` CLI style only after the prerequisite helper contract is stable.

Out of scope:
- No Flow-Lenia, evolutionary search, interactive taxonomy browser, arbitrary kernels, multi-species system, FFT framework, GPU compute, or claims of biological organisms.

title: Add quota-only official limits to tokenusage
description:
## Why

Nova displays official Codex quota by default, but tokenusage 1.5.2 exposes official limits only through commands that still load all local usage history. On the investigated machine that means discovering a 4.9 GiB Codex session tree, reading a roughly 40 MiB parse cache, and potentially rewriting the full cache even when the caller needs only rate-limit percentages and reset times. Tokenusage already owns Codex OAuth refresh and app-server fallback, so the no-history capability belongs there rather than in Yazelix.

## Evidence

- `packaging/tokenusage.nix:4-13` pins the current crates.io release, tokenusage 1.5.2.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/live.rs:50-61` fetches official limits and then unconditionally calls `load_usage`.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/parsing.rs:297-341` discovers sources, loads the incremental cache, parses files, and rewrites the cache when dirty.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/parsing.rs:453-491` intentionally walks all Codex JSONL partitions because old sessions can receive new events.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/parsing.rs:1409-1415` serializes and writes the entire JSON cache.
- tokenusage 1.5.2 `src/pipeline/official.rs:180-220,2064-2113` already owns OAuth and Codex app-server fallback.
- The crates.io metadata names `https://github.com/hanbu97/tokenusage`, but that repository returned 404 during investigation. Contributor access and the actual upstream route must be verified before implementation.

## Contract

Tokenusage provides one documented machine-readable command for official Codex limits that completes without discovering local Claude/Codex history and without reading, pruning, or writing `parse-cache-v2.json`. Its JSON includes the same plan, primary/secondary used percentages, reset timestamps, and window durations already exposed as `official_codex`. Authentication refresh and app-server fallback remain tokenusage-owned. Missing authentication or unavailable limits fail predictably without falling back to local history parsing.

The exact CLI spelling may follow upstream conventions, for example `tu limits --provider codex --json` or `tu blocks --official-limits-only --json`, but Yazelix consumption must wait for a released, documented contract.

## Scope

In scope:
- Locate the active tokenusage upstream and confirm whether contributions/releases are possible.
- Add an official-limits-only command or flag that returns before `load_usage`.
- Reuse the existing `fetch_codex_official_limits` implementation and JSON types.
- Add focused tests proving no usage source or incremental cache is touched.
- Publish a tokenusage release with the new CLI contract and record its exact version and source revision.

Out of scope:
- Do not fork tokenusage, vendor its source, patch the crates.io tarball in Yazelix, or copy OAuth/app-server logic into the bar without a separate explicit user decision.
- Do not redesign token reports, caches, GUI/TUI surfaces, provider frameworks, or pricing.
- Do not add a daemon or live monitor.

## Implementation Notes

1. Verify the current upstream and contribution route before editing.
2. Reuse official-limit fetching directly; the new path must not construct usage sources or call `load_usage`.
3. Add no dependencies. The required HTTP, auth, app-server, serde, and Tokio code already exists.
4. Preserve the existing `official_codex` JSON field contract unless upstream chooses a smaller versioned equivalent.
5. Use a temporary XDG cache with a sentinel `parse-cache-v2.json` in tests and prove its bytes and timestamp remain unchanged.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` in the active tokenusage source should exit 0.
- `cargo test` in the active tokenusage source should exit 0.
- With valid Codex authentication and an empty temporary sessions root, the new command should return official limits successfully.
- With a sentinel tokenusage parse cache, running the new command should leave the file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- A Linux trace or equivalent focused test should show no open beneath Codex or Claude session roots.
- The published crate version should expose the documented command through `tu --help` and install through the existing Nix Rust package path.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the active upstream cannot be located or does not accept contributions/releases; record the evidence and ask the user to choose among waiting, an owned fork, or replacing tokenusage.
- Stop if quota-only behavior still calls `load_usage` or touches the incremental parse cache.
- Stop if implementation requires a new authentication owner or provider framework.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S upstream once access exists, risk LOW/MED, confidence HIGH in the technical change and MED in upstream availability. This is not a Beta 4 blocker because the separate safety bead bounds current behavior. Rejected: empty `--codex-sessions-dir`, which tokenusage treats as a new source set and can use to prune the shared cache; direct OAuth duplication in Yazelix; a maintained Nix patch.
acceptance_criteria:
- The active tokenusage upstream and contribution or release route are identified before implementation; if no releasable upstream exists, the bead stops for an explicit user ownership decision.
- A documented machine-readable Codex official-limits command returns the existing plan, percentages, reset timestamps, and window durations without constructing usage sources or calling local-history loading.
- Success and authentication or error paths do not discover session files and do not read, prune, or write parse-cache-v2.json; unavailable limits never fall back to history parsing.
- One focused contract test makes any history-loader call fail, and one sentinel-cache integration check proves the cache bytes and timestamp remain unchanged.
- The upstream format and test suite passes, and a published version exposes the command in tu --help and installs through the existing Yazelix Nix packaging path.

title: Add host-Yazi package variants without bundled Yazi closure
description: Implement the accepted bounded host-Yazi slice from decision yazelix-maw-o4d and GitHub #672. Rename the Mars-free outputs to the uniform package family yazelix[-no-mars][-no-helix][-no-yazi] with no aliases. no-yazi packages must retain yzx-yazi, managed configuration, open/reveal/sidebar/editor/Zellij integration, but contain no runtime reference to pkgs.yazi. Resolve yazi and ya once from the effective runtime PATH for session-producing and Yazi-dependent commands. Missing binaries, failed version probes, and yazi/ya version mismatch are startup failures. A matching pair that differs from the Nova-tested version emits a warning and continues. Route yzx run yazi through the managed wrapper and yzx run ya through the resolved absolute ya. Host installations own optional preview dependencies. Keep the bundled default deterministic and unchanged apart from the package-family rename.
design: Nix remains the package-composition owner. Extend the internal mkYzx inputs with withManagedYazi and generate one source fact containing source, yazi command, ya command, and tested version for yzx. The bundled branch embeds pkgs.yazi paths; the host branch embeds command names only. Rust runtime resolution owns command lookup, executable checks, canonical paths, normalized version probes, pair validation, and warnings. Runtime apply exports YZX_YAZI_BIN and YZX_YA so yzx-yazi and all yzx-open helpers consume the same pair without re-resolving. The private yzx-yazi launcher must require YZX_YAZI_BIN instead of embedding pkgs.yazi. Home Manager keeps only programs.yazelix.package. Do not add a generic registry, builder, source option, shell sourcing, explicit host path option, or compatibility alias.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Eight explicit package outputs exist under yazelix[-no-mars][-no-helix][-no-yazi], and runtime/runtime-no-helix aliases do not exist. 2. Existing bundled outputs still launch locked Yazi and pass existing contracts. 3. Every no-yazi output has no reference path to the locked pkgs.yazi output. 4. A valid host yazi/ya pair is canonicalized once and used by layouts, popups, opener follow, reveal, sidebar refresh, yzx run yazi, and yzx run ya. 5. Missing, non-executable, unprobeable, or pair-mismatched binaries fail actionably. 6. A matching pair different from the tested version warns and continues. 7. Doctor reports selected source, lookup PATH, resolved paths, pair version, and tested version. 8. Unrelated yzx run commands and recovery commands do not require Yazi preflight. 9. Home Manager documentation demonstrates package selection plus user-owned pkgs.yazi. 10. README LOC scorecard and CHANGELOG reflect the package/runtime contract. 11. Focused Rust checks, nix flake check, flake show, package builds, closure/reference checks, and temporary profile installation pass for the changed surface.
notes: Implemented the accepted eight-output package matrix with no runtime aliases. Host-Yazi variants retain Nova integration while resolving canonical yazi/ya paths, rejecting missing/unprobeable/mismatched pairs, warning for matching untested versions, pinning a complete inherited pair across session children, and ignoring a partial legacy private pair in favor of fresh PATH resolution. Home Manager continues to use programs.yazelix.package plus user-owned pkgs.yazi. Final x86_64-linux measurements: yazelix 2,447,857,424 bytes / 619 paths; yazelix-no-yazi 2,044,345,752 / 500; yazelix-no-mars 1,475,471,032 / 591; yazelix-no-mars-no-yazi 1,049,301,704 / 460; minimal 754,017,176 / 162. Managed-Yazi removal saves 403,511,672 bytes (384.8 MiB) with Mars and 426,169,328 bytes (406.4 MiB) without Mars. Verification passed: six Rust launcher tests, focused host-Yazi/no-Mars/no-Helix/bundled contracts, all 34 compatible local flake checks, Home Manager, real locked yazi/ya smoke, all-system flake evaluation, all eight package realizations, default build, YAML parse, diff/LOC/stale-name guards, and default plus minimal temporary profile installs.
close_reason: Implemented and verified the explicit package matrix and bounded host-Yazi runtime contract.

title: Evaluate workspace-root pane creation and Alt m policy
description:
## Question

Should plain `Alt m` continue using native Zellij `NewPane`, which inherits the current pane cwd, or should Yazelix offer a workspace-root pane action?

The current behavior is acceptable and familiar, but the focused pane can be Yazi in a deeply nested directory, a shell after `cd`, or a locally drifted editor. The pane orchestrator already exposes `open_workspace_terminal`, so a workspace-centric action may be useful without changing how all panes behave.

## Evaluate

- Keep current `Alt m -> NewPane` unchanged.
- Replace `Alt m` with an orchestrator-owned workspace-root terminal.
- Preserve `Alt m` and add a separate command/key/menu action.
- Add a setting only if dogfooding demonstrates durable demand for both defaults.
- Behavior before an explicit workspace exists, after a retarget, with Yazi focused below the root, and with shell/Helix pane-local drift.
- Whether the workspace action should open the configured shell and how it should interact with layouts, floating panes, and pane focus.
- Relationship to packaged `:yzx-new-shell`, which intentionally opens at the current file directory when a file exists; do not erase that distinct file-local workflow without evidence.

## Guardrails

- This is a decision bead, not authorization to change `Alt m` or add a setting.
- Reuse the orchestrator workspace root and existing terminal-opening action.
- Do not force existing panes to change cwd or make focused-pane cwd canonical.
- Do not add multiple near-duplicate bindings without a clear discoverability story.
- Current native behavior remains the baseline if no option is clearly better.

## Outcome

Record the preferred policy, key/command surface if any, bootstrap behavior, and rejected alternatives. Create an implementation bead only after the maintainer chooses a direction.
acceptance_criteria: The bead closes with a documented choice among keeping native Alt-m, replacing it with workspace-root pane creation, or adding a separate surface. The decision is dogfooded from nested Yazi, drifted shell/editor, bootstrap, and explicit-retarget states; it identifies the orchestrator action to reuse and does not add a setting or keybinding by itself.

title: Make new managed Yazi panes follow Yazelix appearance
description:
## Why

Managed upstream/nixpkgs Yazi already has separate dark/light flavor choices and selects one from terminal background at startup, but it does not currently update its stored emulator mode when the host appearance changes. Extending the root appearance system to Yazi requires an owner decision because the sibling Yazelix Yazi fork is archived and not in the runtime graph.

## Evidence

- `crates/yzx-config/src/yazi_config.rs:23-84` already exposes native `flavor.dark` and `flavor.light` pickers.
- Upstream Yazi `yazi-emulator/src/emulator.rs:20-205` determines one startup `light` boolean from OSC 11 background luma.
- Upstream Yazi `yazi-actor/src/app/theme.rs:12-23` can rebuild and overlay the current flavor but reads the startup emulator value.
- The Yazelix Zellij fork native dark/light actions already converge on `HostTerminalThemeChanged` and forward DSR 997 to subscribed panes, so a future Yazi path can reuse Zellij-owned propagation without requiring Mars CSI 2031 in the initial chain.
- `../yazelix-yazi/README.md` declares the local fork archived and superseded by upstream/nixpkgs Yazi plus maintained assets.

## Decision contract

Determine the smallest owner-correct path for Yazi to switch `flavor.dark` / `flavor.light` live when its host reports a mode change. Compare: current upstream capability, an upstream contribution, waiting for upstream, a bounded launcher/restart contract, or a new maintained fork only with explicit maintainer approval. Preserve existing flavor ownership and do not make Yazelix parse/repaint Yazi themes.

## Scope

In scope:
- Check current upstream Yazi documentation, issues, and source for live terminal appearance support.
- Verify whether CSI 2031 can be consumed cleanly through the existing terminal input/event architecture.
- Define startup, live, no-notification-host, and Zellij-forwarded behavior.
- Record the selected owner and create implementation beads only after maintainer approval of any fork or wrapper expansion.

Out of scope:
- No implementation, archived-fork revival, copied Yazi theme logic, polling, forced restart, or new flavor registry in this decision.
- Do not block the initial Mars/Zellij contrast fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The decision cites current upstream source/issue evidence and names one owner.
- A state matrix covers startup dark/light, live transition, unsupported host, custom pair, and Home Manager-owned flavor config.
- Any implementation proposal has focused owner checks plus a Yazelix integration gate and does not duplicate the existing flavor fields.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop before reviving or creating a fork without explicit maintainer choice.
- Stop if the proposal requires Ratconfig to render or classify Yazi palettes.
- Stop if Zellij forwarding or upstream input handling cannot preserve ordinary key input safely.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort S decision; implementation risk unknown until upstream audit. Related to appearance epic `yazelix-5vl-0eg`, but deliberately not a blocker.
design:
Selected design (2026-07-26): keep upstream/nixpkgs Yazi and project root appearance.mode at launch time. The renamed child repository Yazi Bistro is the single flavor-catalog owner. It publishes 22 accepted Classic candidates as exact-revision packages containing flavor.toml, tmtheme.xml, LICENSE, and LICENSE-tmtheme; its catalog owns provenance, explicit dark/light classification, and Catppuccin Latte as the conservative light default. Nova consumes that output and owns only launch policy. On each managed Yazi launch, the launcher supplies the current root mode and Bistro light default to the materializer. An explicit flavor for the selected mode wins. Missing light selects Catppuccin Latte; missing dark preserves native Yazi background detection. When selected, the materializer writes a runtime-only theme.toml with both flavor keys set to that flavor and preserves unrelated theme tables. User and Home Manager source theme.toml files remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Existing processes stay unchanged; sidebar reopen and new popups or tabs follow the current root mode.

Rejected: a Yazi fork, polling, live process mutation, restarting panes, editing user theme.toml, reviving the archived yazelix-yazi fork, the Classic renderer or randomness, and a second flavor owner in Nova. aguirre-matteo/nix-yazi-flavors is incomplete for this catalog, lacks mode classification, lags relevant pins, and had a failing open addition; awesome-yazi is an index rather than an asset package. Neon was rejected because the current upstream asset is incompatible with the pinned Yazi parser. Monokai was rejected because its upstream license files are empty. Synthwave84 uses its compatible maintained fork revision.
acceptance_criteria: Yazi Bistro publishes all 22 accepted flavors as complete pinned packages with flavor.toml, tmtheme.xml, LICENSE, and LICENSE-tmtheme, plus one dark/light catalog and Catppuccin Latte light default. Nova consumes the child-owned output and has no separate packaged flavor owner. Ratconfig offers packaged flavors in 17 dark and 5 light pools; user-installed unclassified flavors remain selectable in both. Each managed Yazi launch projects appearance.mode into runtime-only theme.toml: explicit dark/light choices win, light omission inherits Catppuccin Latte, and missing dark keeps native Yazi detection. Home Manager and ordinary user theme.toml sources remain unchanged. Existing Yazi processes are not restarted or mutated. Focused Rust and Nix checks cover dark/light projection, source preservation, no-user-config light launch, missing-dark fallback, every bundled flavor, and pinned-Yazi parsing. README, configuration docs, architecture, changelog, and LOC scorecard describe the current contract. Full runtime flake checks pass and the installed runtime is refreshed.
notes: Follow-up (2026-07-26): Ratconfig presents a virtual 'default' as the first dark-flavor choice and as the inherited dark value. Choosing it removes flavor.dark so native Yazi owns the preset; Yazelix never writes the invalid literal dark = "default" for that action. The UI action uses a non-string internal value so a real user-installed default.yazi flavor remains distinct as 'default (installed flavor)'. Installed Bistro/user flavors remain the only explicit dark names, while the light fallback remains Catppuccin Latte. Covered by the existing Yazi native-config contract test.
close_reason: Implemented launch-time Yazi appearance following with Yazi Bistro as the sole 22-flavor catalog owner, separate 17 dark/5 light Ratconfig pools, Catppuccin Latte light fallback, native dark fallback, runtime-only projection, unchanged user/Home Manager sources, complete docs, passing focused and full flake checks, isolated install, and refreshed installed runtime.

title: Enable automatic cursors in user-owned Ghostty
description:
## Why

Users who run `yzx enter` inside their own Ghostty can use Yazelix cursor shaders, but automatic regeneration requires explicit consent to modify the real user-owned Ghostty config. The shared cursor choice must come from Yazelix Nova's TOML source, not a standalone JSONC registry or Mars config.

## User-Visible Contract

After one explicit previewed consent, Yazelix Nova adds one optional include to the user's actual Ghostty config:

```text
config-file = ?~/.config/yazelix/ghostty/config.ghostty
```

When `yzx enter` runs inside Ghostty, the child-owned generator consumes `~/.config/yazelix/cursors.toml`, refreshes the stable generated include/shaders, and requests Ghostty live reload only if resolved output changed. All open Ghostty surfaces may adopt the newest application-global cursor; per-window independence is intentionally not required. Declining consent leaves Ghostty untouched.

## Evidence

- `runtime/yzx/cli.rs:122-146` provides one host-terminal entrypoint before Zellij starts.
- `runtime/yzx/paths.rs` can identify Ghostty from the terminal environment.
- `../yazelix-cursors/src/lib.rs:51-66` owns the Ghostty target contract.
- The TOML cursor epic makes `~/.config/yazelix/cursors.toml` the shared Nova source.
- Ghostty supports optional includes and application config reload; validate the exact supported route during implementation against current official docs.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reuse the published child package/API and the TOML source introduced by `the completed staging work`.
- Generate a stable Nova-owned Ghostty sidecar and shader directory.
- Add one explicit consent surface showing the exact real-config edit.
- Locate and safely patch a writable user Ghostty config, preserving formatting/permissions and refusing immutable, Nix-store, unsafe symlink, concurrently changed, or ambiguous cases with a copyable manual line.
- Make setup idempotent and avoid duplicate Yazelix includes.
- Regenerate only inside Ghostty and reload only when output changed.
- Keep one strong non-GUI contract check for consent, idempotence, preservation, changed-output gating, and reload selection.
- Update README, ARCHITECTURE, CHANGELOG, and the LOC scorecard.

Out of scope:
- Do not package, launch, wrap, replace, or pin Ghostty.
- Do not add another cursor schema, config file, registry, or random implementation.
- Do not require per-window independence.
- Do not add a daemon, watcher, dispatcher shader, OSC protocol, or background service.
- Do not add Home Manager.
- Do not overwrite unrelated custom shaders or Ghostty settings.

## Implementation Notes

1. Depend on `the completed staging work`; consume `cursors.toml`, never `settings.jsonc`.
2. Keep terminal generation in `yazelix-cursors`; Nova owns consent, path discovery, atomic include insertion, and reload orchestration only.
3. Validate a candidate with the user's Ghostty binary when available.
4. Dependency decision: reuse the packaged child and Rust standard library. Add no Ghostty binding, shader parser, random crate, or config framework.

## Verification

- Focused Rust contract tests should cover consent/no-consent, path choice, exact patch, duplicate handling, immutable refusal, output-change gating, and reload selection.
- `ghostty +validate-config --config-file=<candidate>` should exit 0 when host Ghostty is available; otherwise use a deterministic stub and retain the real manual gate.
- `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, and `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` should succeed.
- Manual dogfood requires explicit maintainer approval before push: consent, observe live global updates, verify fixed selection avoids redundant reload, and verify refusal guidance.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if safe consent requires rewriting the whole Ghostty config.
- Stop if reload requires packaging Ghostty or a long-running helper.
- Stop if child generation is not atomic enough; fix the child rather than mirroring it in Nova.

## Maintenance Notes

Priority remains P3. Estimated net LOC: approximately 120 to 200 with safe automatic consent. Rejected: wrappers, `yzx ghostty`, per-window orchestration, and JSONC.

title: Replace Classic issue diagnostics with Nova status JSON
description:
## Why

The public Yazelix issue form currently asks reporters to run `yzx --version-full`. Nova deliberately removed that Classic-only flag and finalized `yzx status --json` as its bounded machine-readable diagnostic surface. If the canonical repository swaps without updating the issue form, new Nova users will be instructed to run a nonexistent command.

## User Contract

After the canonical Nova cutover, the GitHub issue form asks users to run `yzx status --json` and paste its complete output. If status cannot run, the form asks for the complete error, `yzx --version`, and the install command or flake revision. The placeholder reflects the actual Nova status schema.

## Scope

- Update `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/01_work_item.yml` in the canonical repository during the Nova cutover.
- Replace every active support instruction that names `yzx --version-full` with the Nova-native diagnostic flow.
- Keep the fallback useful when configuration or runtime preparation is itself broken: paste the complete status error, then `yzx --version` and installation provenance.
- Audit current issue templates and contributor/support documentation for the retired flag.
- Keep the wording product-facing as Yazelix Nova / `yzx`; expose no staging-command or staging-repository names.

## Non-goals

- Do not add `--version-full` to Nova.
- Do not expand the stable `status --json` schema solely to imitate Classic runtime identity fields.
- Do not add a compatibility alias, migration path, or duplicate diagnostics owner.
- Do not change historical release notes merely because they mention the old Classic command.

## Implementation Notes

`yzx status --json` is the primary report because it already includes schema version, package version, config/state paths, selected shell/editor/agent facts, and session state. Its failure is also useful evidence; the issue form must explicitly request the full error before falling back to `yzx --version`.

Rust dependency decision: no production or dev crates. This is a GitHub support-surface cutover change and should reuse the finalized CLI contract without runtime code.

## Verification

- Search active issue/support surfaces and prove no Nova-facing instruction invokes `yzx --version-full`.
- Validate the issue form YAML and confirm its placeholder matches the documented `status --json` keys.
- Run the packaged `yzx status --json` and confirm it parses as JSON.
- Force or simulate a status preparation error and confirm the form tells reporters exactly what fallback evidence to paste.
- Confirm `yzx --version-full` was not added to help or routing.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the Nova status schema is being redesigned as part of this documentation slice.
- Stop if the canonical command rename or repository transplant is incomplete; land this atomically with the cutover.
- Stop if the issue form would recommend a command not present in the packaged canonical runtime.
close_reason: Canonical Nova issue diagnostics are live on main: the issue form requests yzx status --json and the documented fallback; no active support surface uses --version-full.

title: Cut over canonical Yazelix and publish Nova beta
description:
## Why

The public product should remain at canonical `luccahuguet/yazelix`, which owns the established community, URLs, issues, releases, and install contract. Nova is a genuine new v1 implementation with a coherent 207-commit lineage. A two-parent merge would make roughly 4,000 Classic and Nova commits reachable from default `main`, defeating the clean-history boundary. The cutover must instead preserve Classic through explicit refs and replace canonical `main` with one complete reviewed Nova lineage under a guarded maintenance window.

## Evidence

- Canonical `luccahuguet/yazelix` has the established public identity; the former development repository is temporary development infrastructure.
- Current Nova history has 207 commits; current Classic history has roughly 3,801 reachable commits.
- `v17.9` is the last ordinary Classic release before broad config/runtime convergence. It includes narrow Nova-inspired terminal slimming but no public Nova transition surface.
- `v17.10` is the first clearly Nova-shaped Classic release; its changelog explicitly prepares native paths for Nova.
- `v17.12` is the corrected final Classic migration and rollback bridge.
- Existing GitHub issues, stars, forks, releases, tags, and repository identity survive a default-branch ref replacement because the repository itself remains canonical.

## User-Visible Contract

Canonical `github:luccahuguet/yazelix` becomes Yazelix Nova `1.0.0-beta.1` and installs `yzx`. Default `main` reports only the Nova lineage plus reviewed canonical cutover commits. A frozen `classic` branch points exactly at `v17.9`. The immutable `v17.12` tag remains the supported Classic migration and rollback artifact; there is no `classic-bridge` branch. Existing Classic tags, releases, issues, stars, forks, and URLs remain available. Existing former-development config and state is ignored and unsupported.

## Scope

In scope:
- Require clean, pushed, recorded source commits in both repositories and record the exact old canonical main SHA.
- Create and push remote `classic` at the peeled `v17.9` commit before changing main; treat it as frozen archival history, not a maintenance line.
- Verify `v17.12` and all historical Classic tags on the canonical remote. Keep v17.12 tag-only.
- Preserve the final pre-cutover Classic main commit through a non-product archival ref when it is not already reachable from v17.12; record that ref in cutover evidence without presenting another supported branch.
- Resolve, close, retarget, or explicitly preserve every open Classic pull request before replacing main.
- Prepare one complete canonical Nova commit on the Nova lineage containing the reviewed runtime tree, canonical metadata, Nova Beads store, issue diagnostics, docs, workflows, and public identity.
- Atomically rename commands, packages, apps, helpers, environment contracts, and development paths from former development commands and paths to canonical `yzx`/Nova and canonical `yazelix` config/state roots.
- Rehearse the full ref transaction in a disposable clone.
- Record branch protection and automation state, open a bounded maintenance window, and replace `refs/heads/main` only with `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/main:<recorded-old-sha>` or the equivalent exact-SHA GitHub API precondition.
- Restore branch protection with the stable Nova `CI / linux` context, validate repository automation, then publish `nova-v1.0.0-beta.1`.
- Publish concise existing-clone guidance that prefers a fresh clone and explains that ordinary pull cannot reconcile the intentional history replacement.

Out of scope:
- No two-parent merge, raw `--force`, orphan commit, repository rename/reuse dance, archived canonical repository, `classic-bridge` branch, or moving Classic feature line.
- No former-development user migration, detector, warning, fallback, import, deletion, or former-development-command alias.
- Do not duplicate or redesign the main-owned v17.12 migration contract.
- Do not make the former development repository private yet or fold unrelated P2/P3 features into beta.

## Implementation Notes

1. Record old canonical main, prepared Nova commit, Nova root, v17.9 peeled commit, v17.12 peeled commit, every preservation ref, repository id, branch protection, required checks, and open PR disposition before mutation.
2. Compose canonical-only GitHub files and release metadata onto the Nova lineage before touching the remote default branch. The reviewed prepared commit must be independently buildable.
3. Rehearse from fresh clones with the same refspecs and exact lease. Prove the final tree and ref graph, including intentional non-ancestry from Classic to Nova main.
4. Push `classic` and any archival preservation ref first. Verify them remotely before the guarded main replacement.
5. Treat any lease mismatch as concurrent change and stop. Never widen the lease or fall back to raw force.
6. Restore protection and run canonical workflows before tagging the beta.
7. Keep the canonical repository id and GitHub control plane; replace only Git refs and reviewed repository content.

## Verification

- Both repositories are clean and pushed immediately before cutover.
- `git rev-parse origin/classic` equals `git rev-parse v17.9^{commit}`.
- `git rev-parse v17.12^{commit}` resolves from the canonical remote and no `classic-bridge` remote ref exists.
- Every recorded pre-swap Classic commit remains reachable from v17.9, v17.12, or the recorded non-product archival ref.
- The exact old main SHA used by force-with-lease matches the remote immediately before replacement.
- Canonical `origin/main` equals the reviewed prepared Nova commit.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor <prepared-nova-commit> origin/main` succeeds.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor v17.12 origin/main` fails, proving Classic is not part of the default-branch history.
- `git rev-list --max-parents=0 origin/main` reports the expected Nova root; `git rev-list --count origin/main` matches the recorded Nova count plus cutover commits rather than the Classic/Nova union.
- Repository id, issues, stars, forks, releases, and historical tags remain attached to canonical `luccahuguet/yazelix`.
- Branch protection requires the exact stable Nova check and a canonical protected-branch run can satisfy it.
- Classic-only issue automation and the one open pre-cutover PR have explicit preserve, replace, retarget, or close dispositions.
- `nix flake check`, `nix flake show --all-systems`, and `nix build .#yazelix --no-link --print-build-logs` pass in canonical main.
- A temporary profile contains `bin/yzx`, contains no former-development-command alias, and passes help, doctor, and status smoke.
- Fresh and Home Manager installs use canonical config/state roots; isolated former-development state is neither read nor changed.
- Version Gate passes and release metadata reports `1.0.0-beta.1` before the tag is pushed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if either worktree or remote changes during rehearsal or execution.
- Stop on any force-with-lease mismatch, missing tag/ref, unresolved open PR, or unpreserved Classic commit.
- Stop if the final tree is not reproducible from the prepared Nova commit before changing canonical main.
- Stop if repository settings cannot be restored, required Nova checks cannot run, or GitHub mappings cannot be repaired in the same window.
- Stop if canonical main depends on the former development flake, reads former-development user state, or contains partial public renames.
- Stop if v17.12 migration/rollback or macOS/Version Gate evidence is unresolved.

## Maintenance Notes

Effort L, risk HIGH, confidence HIGH after rehearsal. Accepted one-time disruption: existing Git clones must re-clone or deliberately realign main. Rejected: two-parent history union, abandoning the canonical repository, rename-and-reuse redirects, raw force, a v17.12 branch, Nova migration, and piecemeal source porting.
